content.text:
Two docs, no code yet. Next I'll check your machine for the Cyberpunk mod setup you mentioned (Steam/GOG/Vortex/MO2 folders, mod archives), plus hardware and tooling, since those change the plan.

I'm recalling Karpathy's idea of using LLMs to maintain a personal markdown-based wiki as a form of external working memory, which could inform how I structure this project's planning documents.

I want to push beyond that original concept, treating the wiki as agentic working memory tracking decisions, open questions, hypotheses, and build state rather than just a static knowledge store. I should also check whether the user has any leftover Cyberpunk mod files somewhere on disk even though the game isn't currently installed, and start lining up technical critique points to challenge assumptions.

On the voting system specifically, the "no LLMs in the realtime loop" latency argument doesn't really hold since there's already a 10-15 second voting window — so I'd rather classify each chat message incrementally as it streams in, mapping it to an action enum via a lightweight local classifier or structured LLM output, and show a live tally bar. This per-message approach is more transparent, attributable, and injection-resistant than aggregating the whole buffer into one opaque classification at the end.

I'm also noting Twitch's native Polls and Predictions APIs exist but are limited (affiliate-only, 2-5 choices), so chat-based voting is more flexible for this use case.

On turn structure: with 4 roles each getting ~30s windows (planning, dice, cinematic, enemy phase), a full round runs 2-3 minutes, but that leaves squads idle 75% of the time while waiting their turn — I'm thinking about interleaving windows so the next squad's planning phase overlaps with the current squad's resolution.

One optimization is to pipeline the window opening for the next role during the current role's cinematic/outcome phase — showing the dice result quickly first, then opening the next window while the cinematic plays. I'd also give inactive squads something to do, like hype-meter reactions or assist tokens, to keep them engaged, while preserving Cyberpunk RED's per-character REF+1d10 initiative system.

On the licensing side, I'm distinguishing R. Talsorian's ownership of the Cyberpunk RED tabletop rules from CDPR's ownership of Cyberpunk 2077, and checking whether CDPR's fan content guidelines permit streaming and monetizing gameplay footage.

For the ruleset itself, I'm double-checking the RED mechanics I'm citing: critical injuries trigger on two or more 6s on damage dice (granting +5 bonus damage), and death saves require rolling a d10 under your BODY stat, with cumulative +1 penalties on repeated saves and a roll of 10 always counting as a failure — I want to make sure I'm stating these correctly without just reproducing rulebook text verbatim.

Other mechanics to note: armor ablation reducing SP on penetration, the HP formula tied to BODY and WILL, aimed headshot penalties with doubled damage, and autofire/suppressive fire rules — the doc seems thin here but these are secondary.

The real standout idea is implementing a provably fair RNG system: commit to a seed hash publicly before the stream, reveal it after, so chat can verify no dice were fudged. That's a strong differentiator worth prioritizing in the rules engine design, alongside tackling the bigger risk of controlling the CP2077 game engine itself.

For CET, I'm confirming Lua calls through CET can spawn entities and teleport them via the game's teleportation facility, but the sandbox restricts file I/O to the mod directory and has no socket support, so real-time communication with an external process has to rely on file-based polling rather than WebSockets, and I need to check whether CET bundles a JSON library or if a mod needs to include its own.

Rayshader's RedHttpClient plugin for RED4ext could let the game act as an HTTP client calling out to middleware, avoiding the need for a server embedded in the game — though I should mark this unverified. As a safer fallback, I'm considering a file-based IPC design where an orchestrator process writes to disk for the game to poll.

For the actual mechanics, the orchestrator would atomically write command files with sequence numbers, which CET polls for every ~100ms, writing back acknowledgments and telemetry — keeping everything within CET's restricted mod directory and using os.replace for atomic writes. Latency is negligible here.

Camera control is the harder problem. CET can't simply spawn a free camera, so I'm weighing options like AMM's Director mode, Freefly-style CET mods, or directly spawning and activating a camera entity in-game.

A known trick is to use the player's FPP camera component and set its local position/orientation offset, which is how freecam mods like Simple Freecam or Freefly work — combined with teleporting the player, hiding their mesh via an invisibility effect, and disabling collision for noclip, so the camera effectively becomes the player's head with configurable FOV.

Other options exist like IGCS's connector tools, but these rely on manual ReShade-style integration and Patreon-gated features, making them less suited for programmatic control than the invisible-player approach. I also need to account for V always being present in the world, and for disabling NPC hostility reactions so they don't respond to the hidden player.

For spawning pawns, I'm weighing CET's built-in entity spawner against Codeware's dynamic entity system, and considering whether AMM exposes an API for controlled NPC spawning rather than relying on manual menu-driven workflows.

Animations are the riskiest piece since NPCs don't easily support arbitrary CET-driven animation; I'm looking at workspot-based pose mods as a more reliable alternative for controlling NPC stances.

For movement and combat behavior, AI command events like move-to and teleport commands seem to be how AMM's director mode steers NPCs, and I'm trying to pin down whether similar commands exist for shooting or targeting.

I'm sketching three layers of control for puppeteering NPCs: workspot poses for reliable static/looping animations via community pose packs, AI commands for movement and combat that are more natural but less deterministic, and direct stat manipulation like kill or status effects plus effect VFX triggers for damage feedback.

The real risk is that genuine combat AI could kill pawns outside the intended staging, so every spawned NPC needs to be made invulnerable and neutral, with all visible outcomes—shooting, hits, deaths—scripted rather than simulated. I'm deciding Phase 0 of the plan must be a feasibility gate: a "Puppet Spike" that proves two NPCs can be spawned, posed, and choreographed before building anything further.

If that fails, I'd fall back to a "Diorama mode"—leaning into poses, camera cuts, VFX, and sound design like a stop-motion graphic novel, which the doc's own jump-cut cinematic principle already supports. I like calling this the "Tableau Engine": every beat is a held pose with a slow push-in camera move rather than full animation, making it far more robust against animation limitations.

Reframing further, the engine becomes a "tableau renderer" where each action resolves into a Beat—a sequence of shots, each combining a camera preset, pose set, VFX, SFX, and duration, authored as templates per outcome. This decouples rules from staging. I'm also weighing pre-rendered AI video options like Sora, but style consistency with in-engine footage and character identity is a real problem, especially for memorials that need to show the specific dead character rather than a generic render—unless I seed the AI video generation with in-engine screenshots for consistency.

A cleaner solution: pre-generate each character's memorial asynchronously in the background right at character creation, caching it so it's ready whenever needed. The poetic framing is that every character's memorial is rendered the moment they're born, which is both practical and thematically fitting.

On the streamer persona question, keeping the voice as human-diegetic with an optional soundboard of pre-recorded lines feels sufficient rather than adding TTS. For chat platform integration, I'm starting to consider Twitch specifically.

For Twitch, I should use EventSub via WebSocket for chat (not IRC/tmi.js, since Twitch has moved chat to EventSub) — specifically `channel.chat.message`, plus EventSub for channel point redemptions. YouTube's Live Chat API relies on polling with costly quota limits, so restricting to Twitch makes sense for the MVP.

For role assignment, I want persistence across sessions via SQLite, with rate-limited role switching (like once per gig) to build loyalty rather than constant churn, plus some handling for lurkers and a "squad comms box" for non-active roles.

When chat velocity is low, I'm thinking an "autopilot persona" system where each character has a personality-driven default behavior, so quiet chats still produce interesting play — and below a certain viewer threshold, the game collapses into a simpler "everyone votes for everyone" mode. With zero viewers, the cabinet could run an attract-mode demo loop, which fits the arcade metaphor nicely.

For enemy AI, I need a deterministic but interesting decision policy — utility AI operating over the same action enum so enemies follow the same rules as players. For narrative content, gigs could be pre-authored by the streamer as YAML data defining scenes, nodes, enemies, objectives, and branching paths.

LLMs could be used offline to help author content, or in a "near-loop" capacity generating flavor text like narrator lines during pre-generation windows — keeping them out of the authoritative decision path for determinism, but allowing them for non-authoritative narration behind a timeout with a canned fallback, off by default. For rendering, overlays would be a browser source web app with multiple routes driven via WebSocket from the orchestrator, and for dice I'm considering a 3D dice library that supports predetermined results.

I need to verify whether the library supports forced outcomes via notation syntax, since the key principle is that RNG resolves first in the authoritative rules engine and the dice animation is purely cosmetic, displaying a predetermined result with commit-reveal fairness. For OBS integration I'd use obs-websocket v5, built into OBS 28+, for scene switching and stinger playback via media sources, with Cyberpunk 2077 captured in borderless/windowed mode through OBS Game Capture and a HUD removal mod to clean up the feed.

Overhead tactical angles pose a problem though, since looking downward in FPP would reveal V's body or legs where the HUD normally hides them — I need a way to make V fully invisible, possibly through an AMM toggle, though I'm not certain that feature exists.

Alternative fixes include offsetting the camera forward of the body, leaning on photo-mode's built-in free camera, or using existing freecam mods like CET's Freefly or IGCS, which already handle player repositioning. I'll flag this as spike question S-03, "clean camera," since there might also be a lower-level route through spawning a dedicated camera entity and activating it via the camera system directly.

I should also note planning considerations: the timeline needs phased milestones with gates, estimated roughly in weeks, and hardware-wise a single PC running the game plus OBS plus the orchestrator simultaneously will be demanding given how heavy CP2077 already is.

I want to check GPU specs for planning purposes, and look into the CP2077 installation and mod setup. Game version matters too since mods break on updates — I should figure out whether they're on Steam or GOG, since GOG allows pinning versions while Steam doesn't fully, and check their library/mod folders for existing installs.

For the wiki design, I'm thinking of a Karpathy-style structure: a raw/ folder for immutable sources, a wiki/ folder for LLM-maintained pages, a schema file like AGENTS.md, and basic ops like ingest, query, and lint, plus index and log files.

Pages would use typed YAML frontmatter capturing type, status, confidence level, evidence links, last-verified date, and dependencies. I'm building in epistemic tiers so engine claims carry confidence tags that spikes can upgrade or refute, with lint checking for pages that depend on refuted facts — essentially truth maintenance. I also want decision records with revisit triggers, a hypothesis-spike-finding loop mirroring the scientific method, and a small now.md file acting as hot working memory for current focus and next actions.

Beyond that, I'm sketching a memory hierarchy across now.md, index.md, individual pages, and raw cold storage — a nice framing for agent context windows. Session handoffs would append to a log and refresh now.md for continuity across sessions, and since frontmatter is machine-readable I could build a tiny CLI for linting broken links, orphan pages, stale facts, and contradictions, plus graph export and a status dashboard — though I should keep the scope realistic and maybe just write a small lint script first.

Now I'm laying out the concrete deliverables: initializing the repo, structuring the wiki directory with a schema file plus seeded pages covering vision, architecture, decisions, spikes, risks, open questions, component specs, game rules, engine facts, and roadmap, and deciding whether to move or copy the user's original documents into an immutable raw sources folder — leaning toward moving them in to keep things clean.

I'm also weighing whether to add a lint script for the wiki and do a quick environment audit for existing mods, and considering whether the plan should include a minimal spike scaffold like a CET mod skeleton for file-based IPC, though I'm cautious about writing API-dependent code without verifying it first.

I'm sketching a concrete Spike 1 kit: a CET mod that polls an inbox file for commands like ping, teleport_player, and get_player_pos, writes results to an outbox, paired with a simple Python sender script, plus a hotkey to capture coordinates — a tangible, testable step toward making the plan real.

I'm weighing whether to also scaffold a full rules engine core now since it's independent of the game and testable immediately, but that's a sizable chunk and the rules details still hinge on decisions not yet made. I think I'll hold off on the rules engine and focus deliverables on the wiki plus the small game spike kit, leaving the rules engine as the next milestone.

Now I should start with environment discovery — finding where CP2077 mods and related files live by checking common locations.

# AGENTS.md — operating schema for the Night City Arcade project

This repo builds a live-streamed, chat-controlled Cyberpunk TTRPG "arcade cabinet" rendered in Cyberpunk 2077.
Its **working memory is the wiki in `wiki/`**. Every agent session reads it, works, and writes back to it.

The wiki is *memory, not law*. It records what we know, how sure we are, and what we decided and why.
Any decision may be overturned: write a superseding ADR that cites evidence. Never silently contradict a page — update it.

---

## 1. Memory hierarchy (read in this order)

| Tier | File | Purpose | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | `wiki/now.md` | Current focus, active gate, next actions, blockers, last handoff | ≤ 80 lines. Rewrite, don't append. |
| L1 | `wiki/index.md` | Catalog of every page with a one-line summary | One line per page |
| L2 | `wiki/**/*.md` | Compiled knowledge: decisions, spikes, design, components, registers | Pages ≤ ~250 lines; split when larger |
| L3 | `raw/**` | Immutable sources and evidence (user docs, prior-project snapshots, logs, web notes) | Never edited. Add new files only. |
| Log | `wiki/log.md` | Append-only timeline of operations | One entry per operation |

Session start: read `wiki/now.md`, then the last ~5 entries of `wiki/log.md`, then pull pages from `wiki/index.md` as needed.
Session end: run **handoff** (§4).

## 2. Page types and frontmatter

Every wiki page except `log.md` starts with YAML frontmatter (flat keys; lists inline as `[a, b]`).

Common keys: `type`, `title`, `status`, `updated` (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional: `depends_on: [F-001, ADR-002]`, `tags`.

| type | Location | Extra keys | status values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decision` | `wiki/decisions/ADR-NNN-slug.md` | `id`, `supersedes`, `revisit_if` | proposed · accepted · superseded · rejected |
| `spike` | `wiki/spikes/S-NN-slug.md` | `id`, `gate` | planned · running · passed · partial · failed |
| `design` | `wiki/design/` | — | draft · stable · retired |
| `component` | `wiki/components/` | — | draft · stable · built · retired |
| `plan` | `wiki/plan/` | — | active · done · retired |
| `source` | `wiki/sources/` | `raw: [paths]` | current · superseded |
| `register` | `wiki/facts.md`, `wiki/risks.md`, `wiki/questions.md` | `stack` (facts only) | active |
| `hub` | `now.md`, `index.md`, `overview.md`, `glossary.md` | — | active |

### Registers (ID'd entries inside one page)

- **Facts** (`wiki/facts.md`): claims about the engine, mods, vendors, host. Heading `### F-NNN — claim`, then lines
  `status:`, `scope:` (stack it was observed on), `evidence:` (raw path, log date, or URL), optional `note:`.
  Status ladder: `hypothesis` → `claimed` (prior notes, no proof) → `documented` (vendor/community docs) →
  `source-read` (we read the mod's code) → `verified` (we observed it ourselves, evidence recorded). Also `refuted`.
  A fact whose `scope` differs from the register's `stack:` line is **stale** until re-verified.
- **Risks** (`wiki/risks.md`): `### R-NN — title` + `likelihood:`, `impact:`, `mitigation:`, `owner:` (spike/phase).
- **Questions** (`wiki/questions.md`): `### Q-NN — question` + `blocks:` (IDs or phase), `default:` (what we assume until answered), `answer:`.

### Linking

Use relative markdown links (`[ADR-002](decisions/ADR-002-transport.md)`). They work in Cursor, GitHub, and Obsidian.
Reference register entries by bare ID (`F-007`, `R-01`, `Q-03`) — lint resolves them.

## 3. Operations

| Op | Trigger | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| **ingest** | New file in `raw/` | Write/refresh a `sources/` summary → update every affected page and register entry → note contradictions explicitly → update `index.md` → log. |
| **query** | A question about the project | Read `now.md` + `index.md` → read pages → answer with links. If the answer is reusable, file it as a page and log it. |
| **spike-report** | An experiment ran (in-game or otherwise) | Fill the spike's *Result* section with raw evidence (save logs/screenshots under `raw/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-*`) → move facts up/down the status ladder → mark dependents (pages whose `depends_on` includes a refuted fact) → update gate status in `plan/roadmap.md` → log. |
| **decide** | A choice with consequences | New ADR (or supersede one: set old `status: superseded`, link both ways) → update affected design/component pages → log. |
| **lint** | Weekly, after big ingests, before handoff | `python tools/wiki.py lint` → fix errors → judge warnings → log. Also look for contradictions the tool can't see. |
| **handoff** | End of every session | Rewrite `now.md` (focus, gate, next 3 actions, blockers, what just changed) → log entry → `python tools/wiki.py lint`. |
| **playtest-ingest** | After any test stream | Session report → `raw/sessions/` → update design pages (pacing, balance, chat behaviour) and risks. |

Log entry format (parseable): `## [YYYY-MM-DD] op | title` followed by short bullets of pages touched.

## 4. Tooling

- `python tools/wiki.py lint` — frontmatter, broken links, unknown IDs, orphans, index coverage, stale facts, pages depending on refuted/stale facts.
- `python tools/wiki.py status` — dashboard: gates, spikes, blocking questions, high risks, fact ladder counts.
- Stdlib only. Extend it when a maintenance chore repeats twice.

## 5. Engineering guardrails (for code work)

- **Never invent game APIs.** Check `wiki/facts.md`, then NativeDB (https://nativedb.red4ext.com) or mod source. Unverified calls must be wrapped in `pcall` and logged.
- The rules engine is pure and deterministic; all randomness comes from the provable dice service ([ADR-006](wiki/decisions/ADR-006-provable-dice.md)).
- No generative LLM in the authoritative path (rules, votes, outcomes). See [ADR-009](wiki/decisions/ADR-009-llm-boundary.md).
- Everything the show does must be reproducible from the event log ([ADR-007](wiki/decisions/ADR-007-event-sourced-ledger.md)).
- Do not write rulebook text from Cyberpunk RED into code, overlays, or docs (IP — see `R-08`).
- When code changes a contract, update `wiki/components/contracts.md` in the same change.

# Night City Arcade — the project on one page

**What it is:** a live broadcast where Twitch chat *is* the crew. Viewers join one of four squads, each piloting one
edgerunner. A deterministic TTRPG engine resolves every action with provably-fair dice. Cyberpunk 2077 is the stage:
pawns, cameras and effects are puppeted to render each outcome as a cut-together TV-style shot sequence.
Death is permanent. The streamer is off-camera: the operator, and the diegetic voice of the crew's handler.

Source vision: [user spec](../raw/user/system-specification.v1.md), [core philosophy](../raw/user/core-philosophy.v1.md) — summarized and critiqued in [sources/src-user-vision](sources/src-user-vision.md).

## The five reframes (what changed from the original spec)

1. **CP2077 is a tableau renderer, not a simulation.** Every outcome is a short authored *beat*: a timeline of
   camera cuts, poses, FX, and kills played inside the game. No game AI or game combat ever decides anything.
   This turns the hardest risk (animation control) into a content problem with a graceful fallback ([ADR-003](decisions/ADR-003-declarative-stage.md)).
2. **The stage is declarative and self-healing.** The orchestrator holds the *desired* scene; the CET mod reports
   *actual* actors; a reconciler diffs and fixes. Game crashes, reloads, despawns → automatic restage ([ADR-003](decisions/ADR-003-declarative-stage.md)).
3. **Votes are per-message, live, and latency-compensated.** Deterministic parsing first, Jev only for free text,
   a visible live tally, windows that account for Twitch broadcast delay, early lock-in, pipelined turns
   ([ADR-004](decisions/ADR-004-intent-pipeline.md), [ADR-010](decisions/ADR-010-show-clock.md)).
4. **"Never fudge" becomes provable.** Seed commitment at stream start, every roll derived by HMAC, seed revealed at
   the end; anyone can verify every roll ([ADR-006](decisions/ADR-006-provable-dice.md)).
5. **The show runs without the game.** The full loop (chat → votes → rules → overlay) runs against a fake stage
   with a 2D tactical feed. It is the dev harness, the CI test, *and* the on-air failover if CP2077 crashes
   ([ADR-008](decisions/ADR-008-stack.md), [components/broadcast](components/broadcast.md)).

## Architecture

```
 Twitch EventSub ──▶ ingest ──▶ intent (L0 parser → Jev) ──▶ vote tally ──┐
                                                                          ▼
 operator console ◀──▶  ORCHESTRATOR (Python asyncio, event-sourced)  ◀── rules core (pure)
                          │        │            │                          dice (HMAC, committed seed)
                          │        │            └──▶ ledger (SQLite event log)
                          │        ▼
                          │   director: outcome → beat template → bound timeline
                          │        ▼
                          │   stage reconciler ──TCP JSON-lines (RedSocket)──▶ CET "Stage" mod ──▶ AMM / game
                          ▼                                                        │ reports: actors, acks, beat.done
                    overlay (browser source, WS)  +  OBS (obs-websocket v5)  ◀──────┘ (game capture)
```

Details: [components/orchestrator](components/orchestrator.md), [components/stage](components/stage.md),
[components/intent](components/intent.md), [components/broadcast](components/broadcast.md),
[components/ledger](components/ledger.md), [components/contracts](components/contracts.md).

## What already exists (inherited from `D:\night-city-live`)

- RedSocket TCP bridge, CET ↔ Python, verified on patch 2.31 (F-001).
- NPC spawn / appearance / despawn through AMM from our own CET mod (F-004).
- AMM entity catalog exported to SQLite: 4,363 entities, 30k appearances, 43,765 workspots (F-012).
- A homebrew ruleset bible written for a single protagonist ([sources/src-night-city-live](sources/src-night-city-live.md)).

## What is unknown (and gates everything)

Camera entities driven from our mod (S-01), pose/animation puppetry (S-02), staged violence (S-03),
operational resilience (S-04), and the performance budget on this PC (S-05). See [plan/roadmap](plan/roadmap.md).

## Design pillars (kept from the original vision)

Chat is the crew · Four seats, horizontal bonds · Transparent dice, permanent death · TV direction via jump cuts ·
The operator stays behind the curtain. Seat 4 is renamed **Face** because "Fixer" is the streamer's persona ([ADR-005](decisions/ADR-005-ruleset.md)).

# Risk register

Ranked by likelihood × impact. Each risk has an owner: the spike or phase that retires it.

### R-01 — NPC puppetry can't sell action (poses don't hold, weapons don't show, kills look wrong)
likelihood: medium
impact: high
mitigation: Tableau design (ADR-003) only needs *held* poses + cuts + FX. Fallback ladder: AI-command animation → workspot pose → frozen pose → stylized "diorama" (static pawns, heavy FX, comic-panel overlays).
owner: S-02, S-03

### R-02 — Camera entities can't be spawned/driven from our mod (see F-006 vs F-007 contradiction)
likelihood: low
impact: critical
mitigation: Call AMM's own Camera module via `GetMod("AppearanceMenuMod")`; fallback: player FPP camera on an invisible, collision-free V (teleport V = move camera).
owner: S-01

### R-03 — Scenery degrades or NPCs vanish when the camera is far from V (streaming radius)
likelihood: medium
impact: high
mitigation: Each scene manifest has a `player_park` point inside the set, out of all camera frusta (F-009).
owner: S-01

### R-04 — A game or mod update breaks the stack before a show
likelihood: medium
impact: high
mitigation: Steam "update only on launch", back up the verified mod layer + exe after each verification, preflight smoke test before every show, failover 2D feed. If owned on GOG, use the GOG offline installer for true pinning (Q-05).
owner: Phase 0, S-04

### R-05 — Too few viewers for four squads
likelihood: high
impact: high
mitigation: Adaptive squad merge (below N active voters, everyone votes for every seat), attract mode, bot-backfilled defaults that pick the *character's* personality action, not "take cover".
owner: design/squads-and-voting

### R-06 — Broadcast delay makes vote windows unfair or confusing
likelihood: high
impact: medium
mitigation: Latency-compensated windows + early lock-in (ADR-010), measured delay (S-06).
owner: S-06

### R-07 — Permadeath tuned wrong (party wipes → churn, or no deaths → no stakes)
likelihood: high
impact: high
mitigation: Balance simulator with bot chats; target band set before launch; tune only between seasons, never mid-show.
owner: Phase 2

### R-08 — IP: Cyberpunk RED rules/text (R. Talsorian) and monetization
likelihood: medium
impact: high
mitigation: RED-shaped homebrew with original names and tables, no rulebook text anywhere, no paid effects on rules in Season 0, Streamer Mode for music. CDPR fan-content guidelines permit monetized videos of the game. Contact R. Talsorian before monetizing (Q-02).
owner: ADR-005

### R-09 — PC can't run CP2077 + OBS + overlays + orchestrator together (16 GB RAM, 8 GB VRAM)
likelihood: medium
impact: high
mitigation: 1080p DLSS Quality, no path tracing, 60 fps cap, NVENC encode, minimal browser sources (one overlay page). Upgrade to 32 GB RAM as cheapest insurance.
owner: S-05

### R-10 — CP2077 crashes or desyncs live
likelihood: medium
impact: high
mitigation: Event-sourced state (ADR-007), auto-cut to diegetic "SIGNAL LOST" scene + 2D tactical feed, restage via reconciler on reconnect.
owner: S-04, components/stage

### R-11 — Operator overload (voicing the handler while running ops)
likelihood: medium
impact: medium
mitigation: Normal loop needs zero operator input. Operator console with cue cards, a few hot actions (pause, restage, BRB) on hotkeys or a Stream Deck.
owner: components/broadcast

### R-12 — Chat abuse: brigading, alt accounts, spam, offensive names in MVP banners
likelihood: medium
impact: medium
mitigation: One vote per account per window, squad lock per stream, minimum account age/follow time for squad join, MVP banner only shows names past Twitch AutoMod, operator ban hotkey.
owner: components/intent

### R-13 — Jev outage, pricing, or accuracy problems
likelihood: low
impact: low
mitigation: Jev is an enhancement. The deterministic L0 parser alone runs the show.
owner: S-07

likelihood: high
impact: high
mitigation: Hard gates in the roadmap, `now.md` discipline, a vertical slice before any content expansion.
owner: plan/roadmap

title: This repo is canonical; night-city-live is an upstream to port from, not to continue

# ADR-001 — Canonical repo

**Context.** Three folders hold versions of this idea: `D:\cypher-vision` (shelved), `D:\night-city-live` (working bridge,
single-protagonist LLM-GM vision), and this repo (arcade-cabinet vision). The 2026-06 handoff shows a regression
caused by editing the wrong copy.

**Decision.** `c:\Users\bento\Desktop\cp2077-vtt` is the only place work happens. From night-city-live we **port**
(not copy wholesale): the RedSocket client loop, the AMM spawn adapter, `cypher_json.lua`/`Cron.lua`, the catalog
SQLite builder, and the hard-won CET lessons (now facts F-001…F-013). The prior docs are frozen in `raw/night-city-live/`.

**Consequences.** The CET mod gets a new name (`ArcadeStage`) and a new protocol version (`stage.v1`), so the old and
new mods can never be confused in the game folder. night-city-live stays read-only.

**Rejected.** Continuing night-city-live in place: its docs encode a different product (LLM GM, one Chat-V, Ollama in the loop).

type: decision
id: ADR-002
title: Game transport is RedSocket TCP with JSON lines (replaces action_event.json polling)
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
supersedes: spec §4D "CET listens on onUpdate for action_event.json"
revisit_if: RedSocket breaks on a future patch and isn't updated within 2 weeks
depends_on: [F-001, F-002]

# ADR-002 — Transport

**Context.** The spec polls a JSON file every frame. CET's file I/O is sandboxed to the mod folder, file polling needs
atomic-rename discipline, and it has no back-channel. RedSocket TCP is already verified on 2.31 (F-001).

**Decision.**
- Python orchestrator = TCP server on `127.0.0.1:2077`; CET `ArcadeStage` mod = client.
- One JSON object per line; envelope `{type, v:"stage.v1", id, op, args}`; game replies with `ack`/`report` messages ([contracts](../components/contracts.md)).
- CET retries the connection with backoff, so start order no longer matters (verify in S-04).
- Whole beat timelines are sent at once and **timed inside the game** (Cron), so network jitter never affects cut timing.

**Fallback.** File-drop transport (`inbox/NNNN.json`, written with atomic rename) behind the same interface, kept for emergencies only.

---
type: decision
id: ADR-003
title: Declarative stage + beat timelines (the tableau model)
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
revisit_if: S-02/S-03 show live AI animation is reliable enough to drive directly
depends_on: [F-004, F-007, F-008, F-011]

# ADR-003 — The stage is declarative; action is told in beats

**Context.** The spec sends imperative one-shot payloads ("snap actor, trigger firing anim, cut camera"). Imperative
commands drift: a crash, reload, or failed spawn leaves the game in an unknown state (F-011). Also, CP2077 NPC
animation control is the project's biggest unknown (R-01).

**Decision.** Two layers:

1. **Baseline (declarative).** The orchestrator owns a `StageSpec`: scene id, weather/time, V's park point, the set
   of cameras, and each actor's {record, appearance, node, pose, weapon, alive/dead}. CET reports what actually exists.
   A reconciler diffs and sends only the corrections. Idempotent: sending the same spec twice does nothing.
2. **Beats (imperative, ephemeral).** An action outcome becomes a timeline of ops at millisecond offsets
   (cut, pose, FX, kill, look-at). CET plays it locally and reports `beat.done`. When the beat ends, the baseline is
   updated to the beat's end state (e.g. the target is now `dead` at its node), so a restage reproduces it.

**Why this optimizes the project.**
- Crash recovery, save/load, and "restage" are the same code path.
- Beats are **data** (authored templates with variants per outcome: miss / hit / crit / kill), so content scales
  without code, and an LLM can help author them offline.
- Jump cuts (spec principle 4) hide every teleport, so nothing needs pathfinding or locomotion.
- The animation risk degrades gracefully: if live animation fails, beats fall back to held poses + FX + cuts.

**Rejected.** Per-frame polling of commands; any use of game combat AI to produce outcomes; navmesh movement.

type: decision
id: ADR-004
title: Per-message intent resolution — deterministic first, Jev for free text, live tally
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
supersedes: spec §4C "ingest aggregated chat buffer as State → one Choice"
revisit_if: S-07 shows Jev accuracy < 85% on our labelled chat corpus or p95 latency > 1 s
depends_on: [F-015]
---

# ADR-004 — Intent pipeline

**Context.** The spec classifies the whole chat buffer once, at window close. That is opaque (chat can't see the vote
moving), unattributable (who gets MVP credit?), easy to game (one long message can dominate the buffer), and it puts a
network call on the critical path. Latency of the classifier doesn't matter anyway: the vote window is 10–15 s.

**Decision.** Classify **each message as it arrives**, during the window:

| Layer | Handles | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| L0 deterministic | `1`–`9`, `!1`, option keywords/aliases, mapped emotes | 0 ms, free |
| L1 Jev `choice` | Free-text messages L0 can't parse; options = current valid actions + `none` (chatter) | async, ~US$0.00003 each |
| Gate | Accept L1 only if confidence ≥ threshold (start 0.6, tune in S-07) | — |

- One vote per account per window; the latest message wins (people change their minds when they see the tally).
- The live tally is broadcast to the overlay on every change, which makes the vote itself a show.
- MVP attribution = accounts whose final vote matched the winner, ordered by how early they committed.
- Ties are broken by a visible tie-break roll from the provable dice service (not by model probability, which viewers can't audit).
- Jev is also useful off the critical path: picking which pre-written handler line or beat variant fits a situation (selection, not generation — ADR-009).

**Consequences.** The show runs fully with L0 only (R-13). Free text becomes a bonus that rewards in-character chat.

id: ADR-005
title: RED-shaped homebrew ruleset for a four-seat party; seat 4 renamed "Face"
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11

# ADR-005 — Ruleset

**Context.** The spec runs Cyberpunk RED rules directly. R. Talsorian's homebrew policy forbids reproducing rules text
and charging for derived content (R-08). The prior project's homebrew ([ruleset bible](../../raw/night-city-live/night-city-live-ruleset-design.md))
fixed the IP problem but abstracted initiative away and assumed a single protagonist. This show needs initiative order:
turn order *is* the squad structure.

**Decision.** Keep RED's *shape* (d10 + stat + specialty vs DV, exploding 10s, armor that chips, a death save each turn
at 0 HP), with original names, numbers, and tables. Concrete draft: [design/ruleset](../design/ruleset.md). All numbers
are v0, set by the balance simulator before launch, and frozen for a season.

**Seat 4 rename.** The streamer's persona is "the Fixer who hands out gigs" (philosophy doc), and seat 4 is also "Fixer".
Two Fixers confuse chat. Seat 4 becomes **Face** (talker, dealmaker, favors). The streamer stays the Fixer/handler.

**Consequences.** No R. Talsorian text, tables, or role-ability names appear anywhere. The overlay shows our own terms.

type: decision
id: ADR-006
title: Provably fair dice via seed commitment and HMAC derivation
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
revisit_if: never (it's cheap); extend only

# ADR-006 — Provable dice

**Context.** "Never fudge the dice" (philosophy doc) is a promise viewers can't check. When a beloved character dies,
some of chat will accuse the operator.

**Decision.**
- At stream start: generate a 256-bit `seed`, publish `commit = SHA-256(seed)` on the overlay and in a chat message.
- Every random draw `i` = HMAC-SHA256(seed, `"{session}:{i}:{purpose}"`), mapped to a die by rejection sampling (no modulo bias).
- `purpose` labels each draw (`init:solo`, `attack:solo:d10`, `damage:solo:d6#2`, `enemy-ai:ganger2`). Enemy decisions use the same stream, so they're auditable too.
- At stream end: reveal `seed` and publish the roll log. A small public verifier script recomputes every roll.
- 3D dice on the overlay are cosmetic. They *display* the already-determined value and never generate one.

**Consequences.** The rules core never calls `random`. Replays are deterministic (ADR-007). Moments like "verify the death roll" become content.

type: decision
id: ADR-007
title: Event-sourced state in SQLite (the Ledger)
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
revisit_if: Event volume makes replay on restart slower than 2 s (add snapshots)
depends_on: []

# ADR-007 — Event-sourced ledger

**Decision.** Every fact the show produces is an append-only event in SQLite: `vote.cast`, `window.closed`,
`roll`, `damage.applied`, `death_save`, `character.flatlined`, `beat.played`, `operator.paused`, … Current state is a
pure fold over events (`rules.apply(state, event)`).

**Gets us.**
- Crash recovery: restart the orchestrator, replay, and it's back in the exact state.
- Audit: the dice log (ADR-006) and vote attribution come straight from the table.
- Highlights: timestamps of crits, deaths, and clutch saves feed VOD clipping and the memorial wall.
- Wiki ingestion: post-show reports are generated from the ledger into `raw/sessions/` (playtest-ingest op).
- Campaign persistence across episodes (characters, eddies, faction heat, viewer service records).

**Shape.** `events(seq INTEGER PK, ts, session_id, type, payload_json)` plus projection tables rebuilt from events. Stdlib `sqlite3`.

type: decision
id: ADR-008
title: Python orchestrator, TypeScript overlay, Lua stage mod, schemas as single source of truth; fake stage first-class
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
revisit_if: Overlay and orchestrator types drift more than once
depends_on: [F-001]

# ADR-008 — Stack

| Part | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator | Python 3.11+, asyncio, `uv`-managed | Existing bridge code and catalog tools; good asyncio TCP/WS; Python 3.11 is installed |
| Schemas | Pydantic v2 models → exported JSON Schema → generated TS types | One definition for wire, ledger, and overlay |
| Overlay | Vite + TypeScript (one page, several layers), WebSocket from the orchestrator | One OBS browser source keeps RAM low (R-09) |
| OBS control | obs-websocket v5 (built into OBS 28+) | Scene switches, media stingers, screenshots for portraits |
| Chat | Twitch EventSub over WebSocket (`channel.chat.message`, channel-point redemptions) | Current Twitch API; IRC is legacy |
| Stage mod | CET Lua (`ArcadeStage`), RedSocket, AMM as a library | Verified path (F-001, F-004) |
| Tests | pytest + hypothesis (rules properties), golden replays, recorded chat fixtures | Determinism makes golden tests trivial |

**Fake stage (first-class).** A Python `FakeStage` speaks `stage.v1` exactly like the CET mod and renders a 2D tactical
view (nodes, pawns, HP, cut markers) in the overlay. Uses:
1. Build and play the whole show while CP2077 isn't installed.
2. CI end-to-end tests.
3. **On-air failover.** If the game drops, OBS cuts to the "tactical feed" and the show goes on.

**Overturns from night-city-live.** Its bans on WebSockets and HTTP were about the *game* transport. The overlay and
OBS legitimately need WebSocket.

id: ADR-009
title: Generative LLMs stay out of the authoritative loop; allowed offline and for selection
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11

# ADR-009 — Where AI is allowed

| Zone | Allowed | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Authoritative (rules, dice, votes, outcomes, state) | **No generative models.** Deterministic code + Jev classification only. | — |
| Selection at runtime | Jev picks among pre-written options | Which handler line, which beat variant, which bark fits |
| Offline authoring | Any LLM / agent | Gig scripts, beat templates, bark pools, lifepath tables, lint of content, scene-manifest drafting |
| Offline media | Video/image/TTS models | Memorial videos, travel stingers, portraits |

**Why.** The spec's instinct is right. Determinism is what makes permadeath fair and replays exact (ADR-006/007). The
prior project's live Ollama director adds latency, cost, and narrative drift for little gain over large pre-written
pools selected in context. Content pools are also reviewable before air (moderation).

type: decision
id: ADR-010
title: Latency-compensated, pipelined show clock with early lock-in
status: accepted
updated: 2026-10-11
supersedes: spec §5 fixed 5-phase sequential clock
revisit_if: Playtests show viewers miss outcomes because the next window overlaps the cinematic

# ADR-010 — Show clock

**Problems with the spec clock.**
1. Twitch viewers see the stream seconds late (F-016). A 12 s window on the server is ~8 s for a viewer, and their last
   votes land after close.
2. Strictly sequential phases (window → roll → cinematic → enemy) leave each squad idle ~75 % of the time and run
   ~25 s per action.
3. Fixed windows waste time when chat agreed in 4 s.

**Decision.**
- **Viewer-time windows.** The server keeps accepting votes for `L` seconds after the on-screen timer hits zero
  (`L` = measured broadcast delay, default 3 s with low-latency mode, set per stream). Votes are timestamped on arrival.
- **Early lock-in.** If the leader holds ≥ 60 % of ≥ N voters, stable for 3 s, the window closes early: "LOCKED IN".
- **Pipelining.** When the next initiative slot is a party seat, its command window opens as the current cinematic
  starts (the dice result is already on screen). Enemy slots never take a window.
- **Adaptive length.** Base 12 s; +3 s if fewer than N votes after 6 s; minimum 6 s.

Timing estimates and the full round diagram: [design/show-clock](../design/show-clock.md).

content.text:
Decisions are written. Next are the game-design pages: show clock, squads and voting, ruleset, permadeath, and campaign. Every rules number is a v0 draft for the balance simulator to tune.

Lint should accept empty depends_on lists, and supersedes should stay free text unless it clearly looks like an ADR ID. Now I'm planning the pages to design: show-clock, squads-and-voting, ruleset, permadeath with memorials, and campaign covering gig structure, downtime, lifepath, and persistence — starting carefully with the ruleset page.

For the ruleset I'm defining six core stats with distinctive names instead of generic terms: IRON for guns, BLADE for melee, GHOST for stealth/evasion/initiative, JACK for netrunning, WRENCH for tech/medicine/devices/vehicles, and TALK for social skills, settling this split so netrunning and repair/medicine don't overlap under one stat.

I'm also roughing out mechanics: seats get a +2 Specialty bonus on signature actions with growth through downtime, checks use d10+STAT+specialty+mods against a DV with custom "Spike" (crit success, roll and add again) and "Glitch" (crit fail, roll and subtract) terms, and I'm sketching a difficulty ladder borrowing structure from Cyberpunk Red's DV scale but with original tier names like Easy, Standard, Hard, Very Hard, and Legendary.

For combat, I'm defining ranged attacks as d10+IRON+spec vs a range-based DV (close/mid/far bands tied to node distance) with cover modifiers, melee as opposed BLADE checks, and I'm starting to assign weapon damage dice like 2d6 for a pistol.

I'm working out damage dice by weapon type (light pistol, heavy pistol, rifle, shotgun, melee with BLADE bonus) and adding a crit mechanic where rolling two sixes gives bonus damage plus an injury — keeping it since mechanics themselves aren't copyrightable even if it echoes familiar systems. Now I'm sketching the armor rule: damage exceeding SP reduces HP and degrades the armor, with headshots treated specially.

For aimed headshots I'm setting a −6 to-hit penalty with double damage after armor, scaling HP off MEAT (base 15 plus 5 per MEAT point, with wounded status at half HP imposing a check penalty). I'm also drafting the death-save mechanic for 0 HP: each turn rolling a d10 against MEAT with an escalating penalty per failed save, tuning the math so it's tense but not instantly lethal.

This creates real stakes — survival odds drop fast over successive turns, making stabilization by a teammate a race against time, with extra damage while flatlining forcing an immediate additional save. I'm also sketching enemy tiers (Mook, Soldier, Elite, Boss) with their own stat blocks and basic AI behavior like targeting the wounded, using cover, and bosses saving their special abilities for key moments.

Now I'm designing role-specific abilities: Solo gets an overclocked extra attack and bonus initiative; Netrunner gets scene-based hacking actions like disabling enemy ranged attacks, hijacking turrets, dealing bonus damage to cyber-enhanced foes, or revealing an enemy's next move to the audience; and Tech/Medtech gets stabilizing, healing, and deployable cover options.

I'm also figuring out the Face role's social actions and the action-generation logic — valid moves are filtered by role, environment, and state, then the overlay curates them down to four numbered choices (always including a defensive one) to keep the arcade feel simple despite reducing pure player freedom.

For targeting, each option pairs an action with a specific target (headshot the boss, suppress gangers, fall back), so the director builds combinations up to that four-option cap. I'm setting rough balance targets too: 4-6 round encounters, 25-35% chance of a character death per gig, and under 3% TPK rate, to be tuned later alongside clock timing and squad-joining mechanics.

Now I'm thinking through squad dynamics — switching costs with cooldowns, a merge rule where thin squads (fewer than 3 active voters) open their seat to all-crew voting with an "OPEN SEAT" banner, and default actions driven by each character's temperament (reckless vs cautious) when nobody votes, which gives characters personality. I'm also considering comms boxes for inactive squads, an assist mechanic, MVP and service record tracking, leaderboards, and rivalries — since Twitch whispers won't work for secret objectives, I'll just make bonus objectives public on the overlay, which actually makes for better drama anyway.

For permadeath, I'm designing the flatline sequence: ragdoll death in-engine with a "FLATLINED" banner in OBS, followed by a memorial combining a pre-rendered video (generated at character creation) with a live HTML epitaph listing name, gigs survived, kills, last roll, who voted for the fatal choice, and the Medtech squad's final action — all feeding into a persistent Afterlife Memorial Wall. Replacement runs through a quick lifepath poll (origin, motivation, enemy) and a pick from three curated pawns, with rookie stats built from templates plus lifepath modifiers. I'm also sketching the pre-generation pipeline: capture a portrait in an in-engine "portrait booth" scene via OBS screenshot, then run it through image-to-video.

For the campaign page, I want to keep gig structure, the downtime lobby at El Coyote Cojo, the eddies/rent economy, heat, and lifepath enemies seeding encounter spawns — all noted briefly for now.

---
type: design
title: Show clock — round structure and timing budget
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-010, F-016]
---

# Show clock

## One party slot (pipelined)

```
 t=0        t=12   t=12+L        t=14.3            t=19
 |--WINDOW--|--L---|             |                 |
 [options + live tally]          |                 |
                    close→resolve(≤0.3s)           |
                    |--DICE 2.0s--|--BEAT 3–6s------|
                                  [next party seat's WINDOW opens here if it acts next]
```
- `L` = broadcast-delay grace (default 3 s). The on-screen timer shows 12 s; the server closes at 12 + L.
- Early lock-in can end the window at ~5–8 s.
- Enemy slot: dice 1.5 s + beat 2–4 s, no window. Consecutive enemies are batched into one "enemy volley" beat (one wide shot plus quick reaction cuts) when they share a target.

## Budget per round (4 seats, 4 enemies)

| Mode | Party slots | Enemy slots | Round |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spec (sequential, 15 s windows) | 4 × ~25 s | 4 × ~5 s | ~120 s |
| This design, no early lock | 4 × ~19 s | 2 volleys × ~5 s | ~85 s |
| This design, typical (early lock + pipelining) | 4 × ~12 s | 2 × ~5 s | **~60 s** |

An encounter of 4–6 rounds runs 4–8 minutes. A gig (approach check, 1–2 encounters, extraction, payout) is ~35–50 minutes,
so a 2-hour show is 2 gigs plus a downtime lobby.

## Camera grammar per slot (default beat skeleton)

1. Window: **ready shot** of the active character (medium, slow push-in via camera blend), overlay shows options.
2. Dice: hold the ready shot. Dice overlay sits over it.
3. Beat: action shot (over-the-shoulder) → impact/reaction shot (target) → **wide** to re-establish geography.
4. Enemy volley: wide → victim close-up.

## Non-combat phases

| Phase | Window | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Approach / skill challenge | 20 s, one per squad in parallel | All four squads vote at once on their own seat's approach |
| Negotiation (Face-led) | 15 s | Other squads may `!assist` |
| Downtime lobby | 45–60 s polls | Spending, upgrades, rent |
| Lifepath (replacement) | 3 × 20 s | Whole crew votes |

---
type: design
title: Squads, joining, voting, and keeping every squad busy
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-004, ADR-010]
---

# Squads and voting

## Seats

| Seat | Command | Signature stat | Identity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solo | `!solo` | IRON | Guns, breach, protection |
| Netrunner | `!net` / `!netrunner` | JACK | Cameras, quickhacks, turrets, lights |
| Tech | `!tech` | WRENCH | Medicine, cover, doors, devices |
| Face | `!face` | TALK | Taunts, deals, favors, negotiation |

## Membership rules
- Join by command or channel-point redemption. One seat per account per stream; one switch allowed per stream (betrayal is content: overlay announces the defector).
- Minimum account age / follow time (configurable) to join, to blunt alt-account brigading (R-12).
- Service record per viewer (ledger): votes cast, MVPs, characters lost, gigs survived. Shown in the lobby and on the memorial wall.

## Voting
- Options are numbered 1–4 (max four, "four buttons per joystick"). Each option is an action + target pair built by the director from rules-legal actions (see [ruleset](ruleset.md)).
- Live tally bars per option; voter count; lock-in indicator.
- Free text ("smoke the boss from the left column") counts through Jev (ADR-004) and gets highlighted in the comms box when it decides the vote: it's rewarded, not just tolerated.

## Low-population behaviour (R-05)
- **Open seat.** If a squad has fewer than `N_min` (default 2) active members in the last 10 min, its window is open to the whole crew, with an "OPEN SEAT" banner. It reverts automatically when the squad refills.
- **Temperament default.** Zero votes → the character acts by its own temperament (reckless / cautious / loyal / greedy, set at creation), picking from its options by a fixed priority. Quiet chat still produces character, not "take cover" loops.
- **Attract mode.** Pre-show and when chat is empty: the cabinet plays itself on a demo gig with temperament defaults and an "INSERT COIN — type !solo !net !tech !face" banner.

## Keeping inactive squads engaged
- **Comms box.** Messages from non-active squads appear in a squad-colored comms feed (spec §4A).
- **Assist (experiment E-1).** During another seat's window, any squad can spend its once-per-encounter Assist if ≥ 50 % of its active members type `!assist` → +2 to that roll. Tests whether cross-squad coordination ("Techs, assist the Solo!") emerges. Kill it if it adds noise.
- **Telegraphed enemy intent.** The Netrunner's Ping shows next round's enemy plan to everyone, so all squads have something to argue about.
- **Squad directives.** Each gig gives each squad a public bonus objective that may conflict (Face: keep the target alive for a bonus; Solo: bounty if he dies), straight from the philosophy doc.

---
type: design
title: Ruleset v0 — RED-shaped homebrew (all numbers provisional, simulator-tuned)
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-005, ADR-006]
---

# Ruleset v0

Original names and numbers (ADR-005). Every number is a knob in `rules/config.toml`, set by the balance simulator,
frozen per season.

## Stats (7, range 2–8 at creation, cap 10)
IRON (guns) · BLADE (melee) · GHOST (stealth, evasion, initiative) · JACK (netrunning) · WRENCH (tech, medicine, devices) · TALK (social) · MEAT (body, HP, death saves)

## Check
`d10 + STAT + Specialty + modifiers ≥ DV`
- **Specialty**: +2 on the seat's signature actions at creation; can grow to +4 through downtime.
- **Spike**: a natural 10 rolls another d10 and adds it (once).
- **Glitch**: a natural 1 rolls another d10 and subtracts it.
- DV ladder: Easy 8 · Standard 12 · Hard 15 · Severe 18 · Mythic 22.
- **Wounded** (HP ≤ half): −2 to all checks.

## Initiative
`d10 + GHOST` (Solo +2). Ties: higher GHOST, then a dice draw. Rolled once per encounter, shown as the initiative rail on the overlay.

## Ranged combat (node graph)
- Base DV by range band between nodes: close 12 · mid 15 · far 18.
- Target cover: half +2, full +4. Blackout (Netrunner): enemy ranged −2.
- **Aimed head shot**: −6 to hit; damage after armor is doubled.
- **Suppress**: no damage; target must pass GHOST DV 15 or lose its next move and be **Pinned** (−2 to attacks).
- Melee: opposed `d10 + BLADE` vs `d10 + max(BLADE, GHOST)`.

## Damage and armor
- Weapons: light pistol 2d6 · heavy pistol 3d6 · rifle 4d6 · shotgun 5d6 (close only) · blade 3d6 · fists 1d6+MEAT/2.
- **Critical**: two or more 6s on damage dice → +5 damage and roll on our injury table (d6, original effects, e.g. *Glass Eye*: −2 IRON).
- **Armor (SP)** per location (body, head): damage > SP → HP loses (damage − SP) and that SP drops by 1. Damage ≤ SP → no HP loss, no chip. The chip is shown on the overlay as a cracking armor bar.

## HP and death
- `HP = 15 + 5 × MEAT` (MEAT 5 → 40).
- At 0 HP → **FLATLINING**: no actions. At the start of each of the character's turns, a death save:
  success if `d10 ≤ MEAT + 1 − n` (n = death saves already made this encounter); a natural 10 always fails.
  Taking damage while flatlining forces an immediate extra save. One failure = **permanent death**.
- **Stabilize** (Tech, WRENCH vs DV 13, +2 with a medkit): ends death saves, sets HP to 1.
- Example, MEAT 5, nobody helps: survive 3 turns ≈ 0.6 × 0.5 × 0.4 = 12 %. The Tech squad's speed decides it.

## Seat abilities (once per encounter unless noted)
| Seat | Ability | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Solo | Overclock | One extra attack this turn at −2 |
| Netrunner | Blackout · Hijack · Short · Ping | From scene `net` affordances: enemy ranged −2 for 2 rounds; take a turret; 2d6 ignoring SP vs a chromed target; reveal next enemy actions |
| Tech | Patch (each ally once) · Deploy cover · Stabilize (unlimited) | Heal 2d6; node cover half → full; see above |
| Face | Taunt · Call a Favor (once per gig) | TALK vs enemy resolve: enemy targets the Face or loses its action; gig-specific NPC intervention for eddies/rep |

## Enemies
| Tier | Atk bonus | HP | SP | Weapon | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mook | +8 | 15 | 4 | 2d6 | Flees at ≤ 5 HP if leader down |
| Soldier | +11 | 25 | 7 | 3d6 | Uses cover |
| Elite | +13 | 35 | 11 | 4d6 | One trick per encounter |
| Boss | +14 | 60 | 13 | 4d6 | Two actions per round; one signature move |

Enemy AI = utility scoring over the same action set (prefer targets that are wounded, in the open, or taunting), with
the provable dice stream as tie-breaker (ADR-006). Deterministic, auditable, and telegraphable by Ping.

## Action generation (replaces per-node `valid_actions` lists)
`options = seat_actions ∩ node_affordances(node.tags) ∩ legal(state)` → ranked → top 4 (always includes one defensive option).
Scene authors tag nodes (`cover:half`, `console:turret`, `door:weldable`, `vantage`), not actions. New actions automatically become available everywhere they make sense.

## Balance targets (simulator, v0)
- Encounter length 4–6 rounds.
- P(at least one permanent death per gig) 25–35 %. P(party wipe per gig) < 3 %.
- Each seat decides ≥ 20 % of encounter outcomes (no dead seats).

---
type: design
title: Permadeath, memorials, and replacement
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-003, ADR-006, ADR-007]
---

# Permadeath

## Flatline sequence (≈ 25 s)
1. Failed death save: the dice overlay holds on the roll, with a "VERIFY: roll #1847" chip (ADR-006).
2. Beat `flatline`: slow blend to the body; the actor goes to its dead state (ragdoll or death pose, per S-03); the scene's color grade desaturates via the overlay.
3. OBS: full-screen **FLATLINED** banner, heartbeat SFX stops.
4. Memorial: this character's pre-rendered vignette plays under a live HTML epitaph with name, handle, gigs survived, kills, last roll, **who voted for the fatal action**, and the Tech squad's last move.
5. Name added to the **Afterlife Wall** (persistent overlay page + lobby screen).

## Memorials are rendered at birth
The spec pre-renders generic memorial clips. A generic clip can't show *this* character, so:
- At character creation, the stage loads a "portrait booth" scene, the orchestrator grabs an OBS screenshot of the pawn,
  and queues an image-to-video job (Hailuo; the workflow already exists in `D:\cppc\docs`) for a 6–10 s noir vignette.
- Stored at `media/memorials/<character_id>.mp4`. Until it's ready, fall back to a slow push on the portrait still.
- Everything that changes with the run (stats, kills, voters) is live HTML on top, so the video never needs regenerating.

## Replacement
- The seat is locked; the whole crew votes three 20 s lifepath polls (origin · motive · enemy). The enemy result seeds future encounters (spec idea, kept).
- Pawn: pick from 3 curated catalog looks per seat (no live appearance validation, F-005).
- Rookie stats = seat template + lifepath modifiers, generated by the dice service on screen.
- The rookie joins at the next encounter boundary, never mid-fight.

---
type: design
title: Gigs, downtime, and campaign persistence
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-007, ADR-009]
---

# Campaign

## Gig anatomy (data file per gig, authored offline)
1. **Briefing** — the handler (streamer, live voice) over a holo-call shot; squad directives revealed.
2. **Approach** — one parallel skill challenge (each squad picks its seat's approach; results modify the encounter: surprise round, enemy count, alarm state).
3. **Encounter(s)** — 1–2 soundstages, combat or negotiation (Face-led, other squads assist).
4. **Extraction** — a short beat; optional Favor; a travel stinger.
5. **Payout** — eddies, rep, heat with the target faction.

## Downtime lobby (between gigs)
- Set: a bar booth (El Coyote Cojo or Afterlife) with all four pawns seated.
- 45–60 s polls: pay rent (or lose a perk), buy gear, cyberware (stat +1 with a downside), heal, train a specialty, or blow it on a party (crew morale: +1 Assist next gig).
- Lobby screens: Afterlife Wall, squad leaderboards, viewer service records.

## Persistence (ledger projections)
Characters (sheet, injuries, gear, history) · crew eddies · faction heat (rising heat adds hunter encounters) · lifepath enemies · viewers' service records · memorials.

## Season structure
Season 0 = 5 soundstages × reusable gig templates (variety comes from enemy mixes, directives, and lifepath hooks). Rules frozen per season ([ruleset](ruleset.md)).

## Soundstage shortlist (Season 0)
Totentanz balcony (spec) · Afterlife back room · Badlands fuel depot (spec) · Kabuki alley (prior project) · a megabuilding corridor. Pick by S-05 performance and low ambient-crowd density.

---
type: component
title: Contracts — scene manifest v2, StageSpec, beats, wire protocol stage.v1, events
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-006, ADR-007]
---

# Contracts

Pydantic models are the source of truth once code exists (ADR-008). This page is the human-readable spec; keep it in sync.

## 1. Scene manifest v2 (`content/scenes/<scene_id>.json`)

Changes vs spec v1: nodes declare **affordances** (tags), not action lists; cameras are entities with blend presets;
there's a `player_park` point (F-009, R-03); actor slots are separated from nodes; edges give range bands.

```json
{
  "scene_id": "totentanz_balcony",
  "location": {"district": "Watson", "teleport": [-1120.4, 1540.2, 42.1]},
  "player_park": {"pos": [-1131.0, 1552.0, 38.5], "note": "under stairs, outside every camera frustum"},
  "world": {"weather": "AcidRain", "hour": 23, "minute": 40, "crowd": "suppress"},
  "nodes": {
    "n_railing":  {"pos": [-1120.4, 1540.2, 42.1], "yaw": 180, "tags": ["cover:half", "vantage"]},
    "n_terminal": {"pos": [-1124.8, 1543.1, 42.1], "yaw": 90,  "tags": ["console:lights", "console:turret"]},
    "n_bar":      {"pos": [-1117.9, 1548.6, 42.1], "yaw": 0,   "tags": ["cover:full"]}
  },
  "edges": [["n_railing", "n_bar", "mid"], ["n_railing", "n_terminal", "close"]],
  "slots": {
    "party":   {"Solo": "n_railing", "Netrunner": "n_terminal", "Tech": "n_bar", "Face": "n_bar"},
    "enemies": [{"id": "boss_royce", "tier": "Boss", "record": "Character.xxx", "appearance": "…", "node": "n_bar"}]
  },
  "cameras": {
    "cam_wide":      {"pos": [-1115.0, 1535.0, 48.0], "rot": [-35, 25, 0], "fov": 70},
    "cam_ots_solo":  {"pos": [-1121.2, 1538.8, 42.7], "rot": [-5, 175, 0], "fov": 45, "follow": "Solo"},
    "cam_react_boss":{"pos": [-1120.0, 1546.0, 42.5], "rot": [0, -10, 0],  "fov": 35}
  }
}
```
Rotations are `[pitch, yaw, roll]` in degrees. Cameras with `follow` are re-derived relative to that actor's node when actors move.

## 2. StageSpec (desired baseline, orchestrator → reconciler)

```json
{"scene_id": "totentanz_balcony", "rev": 42,
 "world": {"weather": "AcidRain", "hour": 23, "minute": 40},
 "player_park": [-1131.0, 1552.0, 38.5],
 "actors": {"solo": {"record": "…", "appearance": "…", "node": "n_railing", "pose": "aim_crouch", "weapon": "rifle", "state": "alive"},
            "boss_royce": {"…": "…", "state": "dead"}},
 "active_camera": "cam_wide"}
```

## 3. Beat timeline (orchestrator → CET, played locally with Cron)

```json
{"beat_id": "b_000317", "template": "ranged.headshot.kill", "duration_ms": 4300,
 "ops": [
  {"t": 0,    "op": "camera.cut",  "cam": "cam_ots_solo", "blend": 0},
  {"t": 0,    "op": "actor.pose",  "actor": "solo", "pose": "aim_stand"},
  {"t": 650,  "op": "fx.spawn",    "fx": "muzzle_rifle", "at": "solo:weapon"},
  {"t": 650,  "op": "cue",         "name": "sfx.rifle_shot"},
  {"t": 700,  "op": "camera.cut",  "cam": "cam_react_boss", "blend": 0},
  {"t": 760,  "op": "actor.kill",  "actor": "boss_royce", "style": "ragdoll"},
  {"t": 2600, "op": "camera.cut",  "cam": "cam_wide", "blend": 1.4}
 ],
 "end_state": {"actors": {"boss_royce": {"state": "dead"}}}}
```
`cue` ops are forwarded to the overlay/OBS (audio and banners live outside the game). Unknown ops are logged and skipped, never fatal.

## 4. Wire protocol `stage.v1` (TCP JSON lines, ADR-002)

Envelope: `{"type": "cmd" | "ack" | "report", "v": "stage.v1", "id": "...", "op": "...", "args": {...}}`

| Direction | op | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| → game | `ping` | Liveness / RTT |
| → game | `scene.load` | Teleport V to `player_park`, set world, spawn the camera rig |
| → game | `actor.ensure` / `actor.remove` | Idempotent per actor (record, appearance, node, pose, weapon, state) |
| → game | `camera.cut` | `{cam, blend}` outside beats (windows, holds) |
| → game | `beat.play` | Timeline above |
| → game | `scout.mark` | Authoring: capture current V or free-camera transform |
| ← game | `hello` | `{mod_version, game_version, amm_version}` on connect |
| ← game | `ack` | `{id, ok, error?}` for every cmd |
| ← game | `report.actors` | Actual registry `{logical_id: {exists, pos, state}}` every 1 s and on change |
| ← game | `report.beat` | `{beat_id, status: done | failed, failed_ops: [...]}` |
| ← game | `report.heartbeat` | 1 Hz: `{fps, player_pos, active_camera}` |

## 5. Ledger events (ADR-007), selection

`session.started{commit}` · `squad.joined` · `window.opened{slot, options}` · `vote.cast{user, option, layer, conf}` ·
`window.closed{tally, winner, tiebreak?}` · `roll{i, purpose, faces, value}` · `check.resolved` · `damage.applied` ·
`armor.chipped` · `death_save` · `character.flatlined` · `character.created` · `beat.played{beat_id, status}` ·
`stage.desynced` · `operator.action` · `session.ended{seed}`

## 6. Overlay state (orchestrator → overlay, WebSocket)
Full snapshot on connect, then JSON-patch deltas: `{phase, slot, timer{ends_at_viewer, server_close_at}, options[], tally{}, party[], enemies[], initiative[], dice?, banners[], comms[], commit}`.

---
type: component
title: Orchestrator — module map and boundaries
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-007, ADR-008]
---

# Orchestrator

Python 3.11 asyncio process. Hexagonal: a pure core with adapters around it.

```
arcade/
  rules/        pure: state, apply(event), legal_actions, resolve(action, dice) → events, enemy_ai   (no I/O, no clock, no random)
  dice/         seed commit, HMAC draws, rejection sampling, roll log, verifier CLI
  show/         the clock: slots, windows (latency grace, early lock), pipelining, phase machine
  intent/       L0 parser, Jev client (async, timeout, circuit breaker), per-user vote book, tally
  ingest/       Twitch EventSub adapter; ChatSim adapter (bot crowds, replays of recorded chat)
  director/     action → beat template choice (variant by outcome) → binding (actors, cameras, nodes) → timeline
  stage/        StageSpec, reconciler, RedSocket server, FakeStage (2D), file-drop fallback
  broadcast/    overlay WebSocket server (snapshot + patches), OBS client (obs-websocket v5)
  ledger/       SQLite event store, projections, session reports → raw/sessions/
  operator/     local console (pause, resume, restage, BRB, ban, set L), Stream Deck HTTP hooks
  sim/          balance simulator (headless: rules + dice + bot policies, 10k encounters/minute)
content/        scenes/*.json, beats/*.json, gigs/*.toml, barks/*.toml, catalog/curated.json
```

## Invariants
- `rules` is the only module that changes game state, and only by emitting events.
- Every external effect (stage, overlay, OBS) is derived from events, so replaying the ledger re-derives them.
- Any adapter can die and restart without corrupting state; the show clock pauses on stage desync > 5 s.

## Test strategy
- Rules: hypothesis property tests (HP never < 0 except flatline semantics, SP never < 0, initiative is a permutation), golden encounter replays from fixed seeds.
- Show clock: simulated time, recorded chat fixtures, latency-grace edge cases.
- End-to-end in CI: ChatSim → orchestrator → FakeStage → overlay snapshot assertions.

---
type: component
title: Stage — the ArcadeStage CET mod, reconciler, scout tool
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-002, ADR-003, F-001, F-003, F-004, F-007, F-008, F-009]
---

# Stage

## ArcadeStage (CET mod, Lua)
Ported from CypherAgent (ADR-001). Files at mod root: `init.lua`, `Cron.lua`, `cypher_json.lua` (F-003).

Modules (single-file at first, split later):
- **link**: RedSocket client, reconnect with backoff, JSON-lines in/out, `hello` on connect.
- **registry**: logical_id → entity handle + last known state; emits `report.actors`.
- **actors**: ensure/remove through AMM spawn (F-004); appearance; teleport to node (F-008); pose; weapon; dead state.
- **rig**: camera rig, one spawned camera entity per preset (F-007); `cut(cam, blend)` = deactivate current, activate target; V hidden and parked (F-009).
- **beats**: timeline player on Cron; per-op `pcall`; reports failures without aborting the beat.
- **scout**: hotkeys for authoring (below).
- **world**: weather/time (AMM or game systems, verify in S-02).

Rules: `onUpdate` only calls `Cron.Update`; every engine call that isn't `verified` in facts is wrapped in `pcall` and logged with op id.

## Reconciler (Python)
Every `report.actors` and on every StageSpec change: diff desired vs actual → `actor.ensure`/`actor.remove` commands,
rate-limited (≤ 4 spawns in flight). Desync (missing actor for > 3 s, or no heartbeat for > 5 s) → `stage.desynced` event →
show clock pauses → OBS cuts to the failover feed until the stage is green again.

## Scout tool (authoring in-game, the content multiplier)
1. Teleport to a location; fly AMM's free camera to frame a shot.
2. Hotkeys: **Mark node** (V's position + yaw → node), **Mark camera** (active camera pos/rot/fov → camera preset), **Mark park**.
3. Each mark is sent as `scout.mark` to the orchestrator, which appends it to `content/scenes/<scene>.draft.json`.
4. Tag nodes in a text editor, run `arcade scene check` (lints: every slot has a node, every camera sees its subject's node, park point not in any frustum).

Target: author a soundstage in under 1 hour. Five stages for Season 0 = one weekend.

---
type: component
title: Intent — chat ingest, parsing, Jev, vote book
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-004, F-015]
---

# Intent

## Ingest
Twitch EventSub WebSocket: `channel.chat.message`, `channel.channel_points_custom_reward_redemption.add`. Each message →
`ChatMsg{user_id, login, ts_arrival, text, badges}`. ChatSim produces the same objects (bot crowds with skill/noise profiles; replays).

## Pipeline per message (during an open window, for the active seat's squad or open seat)
1. Membership check (squad, account-age gate).
2. **L0**: normalize → regex `^!?([1-4])\b` → option keyword/alias table (built per window from option labels: "headshot", "boss", "cover"…) → emote map.
3. **L1** (only if L0 fails and the text is ≥ 3 words): Jev request
   `{"state": "<situation summary> | message: <text>", "questions": {"vote": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which option does this chat message vote for? 'none' if it is not a vote.", "criteria": {"opt1": "...", "opt2": "...", "none": "chatter, jokes, questions, or unrelated"}}}}`
   Accept if `choice != none` and `confidence ≥ θ` (start 0.6). Timeout 1.5 s; circuit breaker after 5 consecutive failures.
4. Vote book: `votes[user] = (option, ts, layer, conf)`; latest wins; broadcast tally.

## Messages from non-active squads
→ comms feed (rate-limited, AutoMod-cleared only), plus `!assist` counting (experiment E-1).

status: draft

# Broadcast

## Overlay (one browser source, layered)
- **Turn HUD**: active seat, options 1–4 with live tally bars, viewer-time countdown, LOCKED IN stamp.
- **Initiative rail**: portraits in order, current slot highlighted, flatline/stabilized states.
- **Party strip**: per seat: HP bar, head/body armor bars that visibly crack on chip, wound state, ability charges.
- **Dice layer**: 3D dice displaying the predetermined value (cosmetic only, ADR-006) + math line `7 + IRON 6 + 2 = 15 vs DV 15 → HIT`.
- **Banners**: MVPs ("Led by @NeonRider, @ZeroCool + 42"), CRIT, FLATLINED, LOCKED IN, OPEN SEAT, INSERT COIN.
- **Comms box**: non-active squads' chat, squad-colored.
- **Fairness chip**: `commit: 3f9a…` always visible; "verify roll #n" deep link after the show.
- **Tactical feed** (failover / FakeStage): 2D node map with pawns, range lines, cover icons; same data, no game needed.

## OBS (obs-websocket v5)
Scenes: `GAME` (game capture + overlay) · `TACTICAL` (failover) · `BRB/SIGNAL LOST` (diegetic) · `MEMORIAL` · `LOBBY` · `ATTRACT`.
The orchestrator switches scenes from events, plays media stingers, and takes portrait screenshots (permadeath pipeline).

## Operator console (local web page on a second monitor)
- Status lights: stage link, heartbeat FPS, Jev, Twitch, OBS, ledger.
- Hot actions: Pause clock · Resume · Restage scene · BRB · Set broadcast delay L · Ban/timeout · End session (reveals seed).
- Cue cards for the handler voice: briefing text, a suggested line per beat (selected from pools, ADR-009).
- No action can change a roll, an outcome, or a vote (by construction: the console has no such endpoints).

status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11

# Ledger

- File: `data/ledger.sqlite` (gitignored), WAL mode, one writer (orchestrator).
- `events(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts_ms INTEGER, session_id TEXT, type TEXT, payload TEXT)` — append-only.
- Projections (rebuildable): `characters`, `viewers`, `squad_members`, `memorials`, `crew` (eddies, heat), `rolls`.
- Snapshots every 500 events per session for fast restart (only if replay > 2 s, ADR-007 revisit).
- **Session report** generator → `raw/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-<session>.md`: pacing stats (window lengths, lock-in rate, votes per window per squad), deaths, crits, Jev hit rate, desync incidents. The wiki ingests it (playtest-ingest op), so design pages learn from every show.

content.text:
Next are the seven feasibility spikes. Each has a hypothesis, an in-game procedure, pass criteria, and a fallback. Then the roadmap with its gates.

I'm laying out the spike plan for S-01 through S-07, each with hypothesis, dependencies, procedure, pass criteria, and fallback, gated behind G1. For S-01, I'm testing the camera rig by spawning a free camera entity in ArcadeStage after init and polling for its entity ID to confirm it exists in-world.

If that fails, I'll check timing issues by retrying the spawn from a Cron callback after session start, or inspect whether AMM exposes a Camera module directly by logging its table keys. The procedure continues: spawning three cameras with distinct transforms and FOV/orientation settings, verifying EulerAngles argument order against NativeDB, then testing hard cuts versus blended transitions between cameras while recording frame-by-frame footage to catch any visible flashes or gaps. I also need to confirm V stays invisible and HUD-free across all camera angles, and check how NPC/LOD streaming behaves at varying distances from V.

For the puppetry test, I'm planning to spawn multiple party members and enemies (including one from a gang record), teleport them into position, apply AMM workspot poses by referencing the anims.lua source directly, then freeze them with neutral attitudes so they hold stable poses for ten minutes without drifting or T-posing. I need to measure spawn latency and build a library of at least a dozen usable poses while confirming at least six actors remain stable throughout the test.

For staged violence, I'm uncertain about the exact kill method — whether to use a Kill() call, ragdoll impulse, a death workspot pose, or AMM's FakeDeathSignal — so I need to check NativeDB for ScriptedPuppet options. I also want to layer in muzzle flash and impact FX from the AMM FX catalog, hit reaction animations, and possibly wound decals, while testing whether AI can fire at a target harmlessly under godmode.

For resilience testing, I'm planning scenarios: correct startup order with CET reconnect, orchestrator restart mid-scene triggering a restage, game crash triggering failover and restage, a 60-minute soak test with beats every 15 seconds checking memory, FPS, and entity leaks, plus checks for unfocused window rendering and closed CET overlay.

For capture and performance, I'm setting up OBS 32 with game capture and NVENC encoding at 1080p60, targeting a 6000 kbps bitrate suitable for streaming.

I'm defining pass criteria: 60fps gameplay (or a stable 30fps) with under 0.5% skipped frames and RAM committed below 14.5GB, plus a determination on whether a RAM upgrade is needed.

For broadcast delay testing, I'm designing a method using a millisecond clock overlay watched via phone and chat bot echo to measure the lag between a displayed timer and viewer message arrival, with the pass criteria being an estimated p90 latency used to set the default delay.

For judge latency, I'm specifying p50/p95 timing and accuracy benchmarks against a labelled 500-message corpus, targeting at least 85% accuracy at 70% coverage with sub-1s p95 latency.

I'm now defining Gate G1 "First Light" as a single command triggering a full 20-second beat sequence across the camera rig at target performance, contingent on earlier spike tests passing, and starting to lay out the roadmap into parallel tracks beginning with Track A's reboot phase leading toward this gate.

Track B then builds the non-game systems (rules, dice, simulation, show clock, chat intent, overlay) up through G2 "Ghost Cabinet", where both tracks merge at G3 "Vertical Slice" for a real unattended Twitch test, culminating in G4 "Season 0 ready" with full soundstages and launch. I'm now sketching rough time estimates in focused days for each phase, starting with Phase 0 and the spikes.

I'm estimating totals around 45-60 focused days, roughly 3-4 months part-time, faster if agents run Track B in parallel. I want to lay out a concrete first-week plan and a "next 10 actions" list in now.md, plus a precise Phase 0 reboot checklist -- starting with verifying which Steam remnant files and folders need to be moved before writing that phase.

For the mod stack, I should note redscript needs the latest GitHub release compatible with 2.31, and I'm unsure whether TweakXL is required for AMM 2.12 — safest to tell the user to check AMM's Nexus requirements tab and install whatever it lists, though the previously verified stack worked without TweakXL. I also want to flag that during Steam install, the user needs to manually pick the D:\SteamLibrary location instead of letting it default to C:.

After installing, I should recommend keeping CypherAgent in mods temporarily for a quick smoke test with the night-city-live bridge before swapping in ArcadeStage later, and suggest renaming/backing up any leftover C: folder to D:\cp2077-stack\ rather than deleting it outright. For game settings I'm trying to recall exactly where Streamer Mode and crowd density toggles live in the menus, though I'm not confident CP2077 has a "pause on focus loss" option.
