type: spike
id: S-01
title: Camera rig — spawn, cut, blend, hide V, streaming radius
status: planned
gate: G1
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [F-006, F-007, F-008, F-009]
---

# S-01 — Camera rig

**Hypothesis.** Our mod can spawn N camera entities (`simple_free_camera.ent`, F-007), place them, and switch with
blend 0 (hard cut) or blend > 0 (move), with V hidden and parked within ~30 m without visible quality loss.

**Procedure** (scratch CET mod `ArcadeSpike`, commands over the existing bridge):
1. In-world, after session start, call `exEntitySpawner.Spawn("base\\entities\\cameras\\simple_free_camera.ent", transform, '')`, then poll `Game.FindEntityByID` every 0.1 s for ≤ 2 s (AMM's pattern, raw/amm/camera.lua). Log whether `exEntitySpawner` is nil **at onInit vs. inside a Cron callback after load**, which tests the timing explanation for F-006.
2. If it's nil in our context: `GetMod("AppearanceMenuMod")` and log the table's keys to find its Camera module; drive that instead (Q-08).
3. Spawn three cameras at hand-picked transforms. `component:SetFOV(f)`; orientation via `EulerAngles.new(...)` → `:ToQuat()` → `SetLocalOrientation` (check EulerAngles constructor argument order on NativeDB first).
4. Hard cut A→B: `A.component:Deactivate(0,false)` then `B.component:Activate(0,false)`. Record OBS at 60 fps and step frames for any FPP flash between them.
5. Blend B→C with 1.5 s. Does it interpolate from B or from the player camera?
6. Hide V: replicate AMM's `Util:AddPlayerEffects()` + `Tools:ToggleHead()` (source-read them first). Check for HUD elements, crosshair, or V's shadow in all shots.
7. Streaming: park V at 5 / 30 / 80 / 150 m from the subject; screenshot each (LOD, NPC presence, collision). Proves or refutes F-009.

**Pass.** Three presets, hard cut with zero intermediate frames, working blend, V invisible (incl. shadow), no HUD, no quality loss with V parked ≤ 30 m.

**Fallback.** (a) AMM's module; (b) the player's FPP camera with V invisible and noclip: teleporting V moves the camera. Cuts become teleports.

## Result
_(not run)_

type: spike
id: S-02
title: Puppetry — 6 actors at nodes, poses, freeze, expressions, weapons, no AI interference
status: planned
gate: G1
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [F-004, F-005, F-008, F-012, F-013]

# S-02 — Puppetry

**Hypothesis.** We can hold six spawned actors (four party, two enemies, at least one gang record via F-005) at authored
nodes in authored poses for 10+ minutes, and change pose on command, without game AI moving them.

**Pre-work (no game).** Source-read the AMM functions behind F-013 in `D:\night-city-live\AppearanceMenuMod\Modules\`
(`anims.lua`, `tools.lua`, `util.lua`) and record the exact call chains as facts. Query the catalog SQLite for
candidate workspots: aim, crouch-aim, typing, hands-up, kneel-injured, lying-dead, talk-gesture, lean, sit-bar.

**Procedure.**
1. Spawn 6 actors (F-004 path, `try_direct_record` for the gang record). Measure command → visible latency.
2. Teleport each to a node with yaw (F-008). Repeat 20×; note snaps, falls, or floating.
3. Apply a workspot pose per actor; then freeze (AMM FreezeNPC) and unfreeze.
4. Expression + look-at on two actors. Equip a weapon on two actors; check it's visible in hand during a pose.
5. Neutralize AI: attitude group friendly/neutral, god mode; confirm no wandering, fleeing, combat, or reactions to each other or to V; confirm passers-by and NCPD ignore the set.
6. Leave it running for 10 minutes and watch for drift, T-poses, despawns.

**Pass.** Six actors stable for 10 min; ≥ 12 usable poses catalogued with tags; spawn latency p95 < 3 s; weapon visible in at least aim poses.

**Fallback.** Fewer pose types plus heavier camera/FX work ("diorama mode", R-01).

## Result
_(not run)_

type: spike
id: S-03
title: Staged violence — gunfire FX, hit reactions, death on command
status: planned
gate: G1
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [F-012, F-013]
---

# S-03 — Staged violence

**Hypothesis.** A 4-second "shot → hit → drop" beat can be built from held poses, FX entities, and a death state, and it
reads clearly with no game combat AI involved.

**Candidates to test (research each in NativeDB/AMM source before calling):**
- Muzzle flash / impact / blood: AMM "FX & Effects" entities (103, F-012) spawned at weapon/target positions and despawned after ~200 ms.
- Death: (a) a lying-dead workspot; (b) killing the puppet and letting it ragdoll; (c) AMM's fake-death approach (named in the brief, unverified). Compare how it looks and whether the body stays put.
- Hit reaction: a stagger pose between shot and death; camera micro-shake via a 0.1 s blend jitter.
- Gun audio comes from the overlay/OBS (cue op), so it's deterministic.

**Procedure.** Build three beats by hand (miss, hit, kill), play each 10× on the same set, record clips. Blind test: show the
clips to 3 people and ask "what happened?"

**Pass.** ≥ 90 % correct reads; the corpse is stable for the rest of the scene (and restageable as `state: dead`).

**Fallback.** Cut away on impact (reaction shot of the shooter + SFX + overlay KILL banner) and reveal the body already in the death pose.

## Result
_(not run)_

type: spike
id: S-04
title: Resilience — reconnect in any order, restage, crash failover, 60-minute soak, unfocused rendering
status: planned
gate: G3
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [F-002, F-010, F-011]

# S-04 — Resilience

**Procedure.**
1. Start the game first, then the orchestrator 60 s later: does the CET backoff loop connect? (Tests whether a failed RedSocket can `Connect()` again; otherwise destroy/recreate the socket.)
2. Kill the orchestrator mid-scene, restart: ledger replay → reconciler restages to identical StageSpec.
3. Kill the game mid-beat: OBS auto-cuts to TACTICAL within 5 s; relaunch → load save → stage reconnects → restage → resume.
4. Soak: 60 min, a beat every 15 s, 6 actors. Track game RAM, FPS, registry count (entity leaks), CET errors.
5. Focus: game unfocused while the operator types in another app on monitor 2 (Q-09). Rendering rate and audio?

**Pass.** All five behave; zero manual steps in 2 beyond relaunching the game; no leak over 60 min.

**Pass.** Game ≥ 55 fps p1 (or a locked 30 fps if it looks fine on stream), OBS skipped frames < 0.5 %, RAM headroom ≥ 1.5 GB.

# S-06 — Broadcast delay

**Procedure.** Test channel, low-latency mode on. The overlay shows a large server clock and a countdown. Two or three
helpers on different devices type `now` the instant the countdown shows 0. The orchestrator logs arrival times.
`L = arrival − server_zero`, which includes typing reaction time (deliberately: that's what a real vote experiences).
Repeat 20 times.

**Pass/output.** p50 and p90 of L; default L = p90, rounded up to 0.5 s; record in ADR-010.

| Gate | Definition of done | Status |

| **G4 Launch** | 5 soundstages, lobby, memorial pipeline, lifepath, cross-episode persistence, stream-day runbook, 3 full rehearsals. | open |

# Source: the user's vision (2026-10-11)

Two docs: the *System Specification* (architecture, subsystems, schemas, guardrails) and *The Core Philosophy* (why: the arcade cabinet, four joysticks, shared stakes).

## Kept as pillars
Arcade-operator paradigm · four squads with turn-gated votes · discrete node graph + jump cuts · no generative LLM in the
real-time loop · transparent dice and permanent death · MVP credit · conflicting squad directives · downtime lobby · lifepath enemies seeding encounters · memorial vault.

## Changed (with reasons)

| Spec item | Now | Why | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_event.json` polled each frame | RedSocket TCP JSON lines | Already verified (F-001), has a back-channel, no file races | ADR-002 |
| Imperative per-action payload | Declarative StageSpec + beat timelines | Crash/reload recovery, content as data, animation-risk fallback | ADR-003 |
| Jev classifies the whole chat buffer at close | Per-message L0 → Jev, live tally | Transparency, attribution, spam resistance, no critical-path call | ADR-004 |
| Tie → Jev probability, then coin | Tie → visible provable roll | Viewers can audit a roll, not a model probability | ADR-004/006 |
| Fixed 10–15 s windows, 5 sequential phases | Viewer-time grace + early lock-in + pipelining | Broadcast delay; ~120 s → ~60 s rounds | ADR-010 |
| Cyberpunk RED rules as-is | RED-shaped homebrew, original names, simulator-tuned | R. Talsorian policy (R-08); tuning is required if you never fudge | ADR-005 |
| Seat 4 "Fixer" | Seat 4 "Face" | Streamer is the Fixer; two Fixers confuse chat | ADR-005 |
| `valid_actions` listed per node | Node affordance tags → generated actions | Authoring cost; consistency | design/ruleset |
| Death save `1d10 ≤ Body` | `d10 ≤ MEAT + 1 − n`, natural 10 fails, Stabilize by Tech | Escalation and team rescue are the drama | design/ruleset |
| Low velocity → auto "take cover" | Open seat + temperament defaults + attract mode | "Take cover" loops are dead air | design/squads-and-voting |
| Pre-rendered generic memorials | Per-character memorial rendered at creation + live epitaph | A generic clip can't show *this* character | design/permadeath |
| Pawn mesh-collapse heartbeat → `AMM.Teleport()` | Reconciler restages from StageSpec | One mechanism for every desync | components/stage |
| IGCS freecam for programmatic cuts | Spawned camera entities | IGCS isn't scriptable externally; AMM's camera entity is (F-007) | S-01 |
| "Complete HUD Remover" | Native HUD toggles + camera entities (HUD likely absent) | Verify in S-01 before adding mods | S-01 |

## Dropped / deferred
YouTube ingest (Q-01) · Sora/Runway generic stingers (replaced by in-engine captures + Hailuo i2v from portraits) ·
"Sub-150 ms" as a requirement (irrelevant inside a 12 s window, ADR-004).

## Added (not in the docs)
Provable dice · event-sourced ledger · FakeStage + tactical failover feed · scout authoring tool · balance simulator ·
latency-compensated windows · operator console with no outcome-changing controls · telegraphed enemy intent · Assist experiment.

## Contradictions found in the source
- Seat 4 = "Fixer" vs streamer = "the Fixer" → resolved by ADR-005.
- Philosophy doc: 4-phase tick; spec: 5 phases → superseded by ADR-010.
- Spec §3 shows IPC as "`action_event.json` / WebSocket"; CET has no native WebSocket → ADR-002.

# Source: Karpathy, "LLM Wiki" (gist, 2026-04-04)

**The pattern.** Three layers: immutable raw sources, an LLM-maintained markdown wiki, and a schema file. Three operations:
ingest, query, lint. Two special files: `index.md` (catalog) and `log.md` (append-only, greppable). Knowledge is
compiled once and kept current, not re-derived per question.

## Adopted as-is
raw/ is immutable · the LLM writes the wiki · `AGENTS.md` is the schema · ingest/query/lint · index + greppable log · Obsidian-compatible links · git as history.

## Extensions for a *project* (his is a knowledge base; ours has to get something built)

| Extension | What it adds | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Memory hierarchy** | `now.md` (L0, rewritten each session) above the index, so any agent resumes in one read | AGENTS.md §1 |
| **Epistemic ladder** | Every engine claim carries hypothesis → claimed → documented → source-read → verified/refuted | facts.md |
| **Version-scoped truth** | Facts record the mod stack they were observed on; a stack change auto-flags them stale | facts.md `stack:`, lint |
| **Truth maintenance** | Pages declare `depends_on`; refuting a fact flags every dependent page | lint |
| **Experiments as first-class pages** | Spikes: hypothesis → procedure → pass criteria → result; the only way facts climb the ladder | spikes/ |
| **Decisions with revisit triggers** | ADRs say what would overturn them; supersession links both ways | decisions/ |
| **Registers with IDs** | Facts / risks / questions as ID'd entries; questions carry `blocks:` and a working `default:` | registers |
| **New operations** | spike-report, decide, handoff, playtest-ingest | AGENTS.md §3 |
| **The product feeds the wiki** | The show's ledger writes session reports into raw/sessions/; design pages learn from every stream | components/ledger |
| **Machine-checkable** | `tools/wiki.py` lint + status dashboard over frontmatter and IDs | tools/ |

Principle kept from the user: the wiki is **working memory, not a design constraint**. It records belief and decisions; it never forbids.

# Glossary

- **Seat** — one of four crew characters: Solo, Netrunner, Tech, Face. **Squad** — the viewers piloting a seat.
- **Handler / Fixer** — the streamer's diegetic persona (off-camera voice).
- **Window** — the vote period for one seat's slot. **Grace (L)** — extra server-side seconds covering broadcast delay.
- **Lock-in** — early window close on clear consensus.
- **Slot** — one entry in the initiative order (party or enemy).
- **Beat** — a short timeline of stage ops (cuts, poses, FX, kills) that renders one outcome. **Beat template** — authored beat with variants (miss/hit/crit/kill).
- **StageSpec** — the declarative desired state of the set; the reconciler makes the game match it.
- **Node** — a tagged point in a scene (cover, console, vantage). **Affordance** — a node tag that enables actions.
- **Player park** — where invisible V waits so the world streams around the set.
- **FakeStage / tactical feed** — the 2D stand-in renderer; dev harness and on-air failover.
- **Ledger** — the event-sourced SQLite store.
- **Commit / reveal** — publish SHA-256(seed) at start, reveal the seed at the end; proves dice weren't fudged.
- **L0 / L1** — deterministic vote parsing / Jev classification of free text.
- **Open seat** — a seat with too few squad members, opened to the whole crew.
- **Temperament** — a character's default behaviour when nobody votes.
- **Flatlining** — 0 HP; death saves each turn until stabilized or dead.
- **Spike / Glitch** — exploding natural 10 / natural 1 on a check.
- **Gate (G1–G4)** — roadmap checkpoints: First Light, Ghost Cabinet, Vertical Slice, Launch.

Now I'm refining stale-fact detection to only compare scopes prefixed with the actual stack name, plus setting severity levels for dependencies on refuted or stale facts versus unverified claims. I'm also working out orphan-page detection — treating index.md as the source of truth for coverage, and flagging pages with no inbound links beyond that as a separate warning.

For the status command, I'm mapping out what gets reported: roadmap gate statuses, spike tracking, unanswered questions, high-risk items, fact counts by confidence level, decision counts, and pages that depend on unverified facts.

content.text:
I've turned your two docs into a staged plan with four go/no-go checkpoints, and built the wiki that serves as the project's working memory. Nothing in the game has been built or tested yet. The plan's first step is reinstalling Cyberpunk and testing the open game-side questions.

## What I found on your machine

- **Your earlier project, `D:\night-city-live`, already proved the hardest connection.** It recorded in-game evidence on patch 2.31 that a Python program can send commands into the game (through the RedSocket mod) and spawn, restyle and despawn NPCs through AMM. That code will be carried over, not rewritten.
- **Scripted camera cuts look possible.** AMM's own source code spawns camera objects and switches between them, either as a hard cut or a smooth move. I read the code; nobody has driven it from our mod yet.
- **Your mods survived the uninstall.** The Steam folder still holds CET, RED4ext, RedSocket, ArchiveXL, Codeware, AMM and your old bridge mod. One piece is gone: redscript, which some of those mods need. Patch 2.31 is still the current version, so the April setup should come back unchanged.
- **Install the game to D:, not C:.** C: has only 101 GB free; D: has 3.4 TB.
- **RAM is the tight spot.** 16 GB for the game, OBS and the overlays together is marginal. A 32 GB upgrade is the cheapest insurance; one of the tests settles whether you need it.

## Main changes to your spec

- **The game only renders.** Every outcome is a short scripted sequence of camera cuts, poses, effects and kills. No game AI or game combat decides anything. If NPC animation turns out limited, this degrades to held poses plus cuts instead of failing.
- **The stage repairs itself.** The controller keeps a description of how the scene should look and fixes any difference, so crashes and reloads recover automatically.
- **Votes are counted message by message, with a live tally on screen.** Typed numbers and keywords are parsed directly; Jev (it exists, and costs a fraction of a cent per call) only handles free-text messages. Vote windows allow for Twitch's few-second delay and close early when chat agrees. Rounds come out around 60 seconds instead of 120.
- **Fair dice you can prove.** A hash of the random seed is published at stream start and the seed is revealed at the end, so anyone can re-check every roll.
- **The rules keep Cyberpunk RED's structure, with original names and numbers.** That avoids R. Talsorian's rules on reusing their text. A simulator tunes the numbers before launch, since you can't adjust anything during a show.
- **Seat 4 is now "Face".** You're the Fixer; two Fixers would confuse chat.
- **The show runs without the game.** A 2D tactical view stands in for Cyberpunk. It lets the software be built now while the game downloads, and it becomes the on-air backup if the game crashes.

## The wiki

It follows Karpathy's structure: immutable sources in `raw/`, compiled pages in `wiki/`, and the rules for agents in `AGENTS.md`. On top of that:

- **A start-here page.** Any session resumes from `wiki/now.md` in one read.

You picked Twitch only, no paid effects on rules or dice, and Steam for now. I'll record those answers in the wiki, then build the rules core, the provable dice, and the balance simulator.

I'm noting the decisions: Twitch only, no paid effects, Steam acceptable with mitigations over GOG. Now I'll record these in the wiki and move on to building the rules core, dice, and sim, starting with setting up the project structure.

For the dice module, I'm designing a deterministic HMAC-based roller — a Dice class tracking seed, session ID, and counter, with commit/draw/verify functions using rejection sampling on hash output to produce fair rolls that can later be independently verified against a logged seed.

For the rules module, I'm sketching a Config dataclass holding all the tunable knobs (DV ladder, cover mods, HP formula, penalties, crit bonuses, etc.), loaded from a TOML file.

Now I'm defining the data model: Stats and Character classes capturing stats, specialty, HP, armor points, weapon, status, death saves, and position, plus an Enemy variant and a unified Combatant abstraction spanning party and enemy sides. I also need a weapons table, a check resolver for rolling against a base difficulty with spike/glitch handling, and a combat resolver covering the core v0 action set — attacks, suppression, stabilizing, patching, cover, overclocking, and similar maneuvers — while trimming down the full action list to something manageable for the simulator.

For the encounter state I'm tracking combatants, initiative order, round and turn counters, environment flags like blackout duration, and a log. I'm leaning toward an event-sourced design where resolving an action returns a list of events that get folded into state, keeping the core resolve function pure and simple.

For range, rather than a full node graph I'm abstracting it into range bands per combatant pair, with a default like "mid" and overrides where needed. For enemy AI, I'm thinking through a utility-scoring approach to pick actions.

Enemies should target visible, living party members, preferring low HP and exposed targets, but with a configurable weight for whether to finish off flatlining characters since that's brutal. Bosses get two actions, and mooks should flee and leave combat once their leader falls and their HP drops low enough.

For death saves, I'm defining the per-turn logic for flatlining characters — a roll against MEAT with decreasing odds each failed attempt, a natural 10 as an automatic fail, and taking damage while down triggering an immediate extra save.

Stabilizing requires a WRENCH check against a difficulty value, improved by medkit charges, which resets the character to ALIVE with 1 HP (wounded and acting at a penalty). I'm also working out wound penalties at half HP, and the damage/armor resolution — rolling weapon dice with crit detection on multiple sixes, then applying armor soak per location with extra damage for headshots and armor degrading on hits that exceed its protection.

For critical hits, I'm deciding the bonus damage bypasses armor entirely and applies straight to HP, which I'll note needs updating in the ruleset doc. I'm also drafting the injury table with specific stat penalties tied to each result — like a glass eye reducing IRON, cracked ribs giving a flat penalty to all checks, burns hitting BLADE and IRON, concussions hurting JACK and TALK, and shrapnel wounds draining GHOST.

Beyond that, I'm working out initiative (d10 plus GHOST, with Solo bonus), building default seat templates with stats for each character slot, and setting enemy tiers with their attack bonus, HP, SP, weapon dice, and GHOST values scaling from Mook to Boss. I'm also figuring out difficulty values for attacks in both directions, factoring in range, cover, and a blackout penalty affecting enemies.

Now I'm defining special combat actions: Suppress (a GHOST check to avoid being pinned), Taunt (a TALK check forcing an enemy to target the Face), Blackout (a JACK check that debuffs enemy ranged attacks for two rounds), and Short (a JACK check that lets an attack bypass SP) — trying to balance these as limited-use netrunner abilities tied to encounter resources.

I'm also sketching out support abilities like Patch (a WRENCH-based heal, deciding whether it should auto-succeed or require a DV check without consuming the use on failure), Deploy Cover (granting an ally full cover once per encounter), and Take Cover as a self-targeted defensive option.

Cover state should probably persist once taken rather than being purely positional, which keeps things tactical since both players and enemies like Soldiers can use it. I'm also adding Overclock, letting a character make two attacks at a penalty once per encounter.

Given how much is being requested, I'm aiming to implement a reasonably complete v0 with a clean action structure — defining an Action type with fields for kind, actor, target, and whether it's aimed — plus a function to generate the list of legal actions available to any given actor, and a simplified "Director's top options" heuristic for AI decision-making.

For the simulation layer, I'm sketching bot policies for the party — a "crowd" policy that approximates aggregated chat behavior through noisy heuristic utility, plus some temperament-based variants. A "gig" is defined as a sequence of encounters where party HP carries over but doesn't heal between fights except for stabilization. I'm defining metrics to track: rounds per encounter, probability of at least one death or a full wipe per gig, and each seat's share of "decisive" contributions — measured via damage dealt, stabilizations, and debuffs — to verify every seat meaningfully influences at least 20% of outcomes.

I'm weighting impact points as damage dealt plus bonuses for stabilizes and successful control effects like taunt, suppress, or blackout, tracking damage share and rescues separately to flag any seat falling below 10% contribution. For encounter generation, I'm setting up enemy composition tiers (standard, hard, boss mixes) with randomized range bands and cover placement, then building a CLI entry point to run these simulations.

Checking HMAC-based dice roll speed in Python, estimating roughly 1-3 microseconds per draw with the fast C path, which scales to about 3.2 million draws across 10,000 gigs — manageable in 5-10 seconds. I'm deciding to keep the same Dice interface for both simulation and real use to guarantee identical code paths, while considering a FastDice variant using plain random for cases where HMAC overhead isn't needed.

I'm outlining the test suite: dice tests covering determinism, commit/verify, uniformity, rejection sampling, and tamper detection; rules tests using hypothesis for invariants like HP/SP never going negative, initiative ordering, death saves, armor ablation, crits, and stabilization; plus a smoke test running 200 gigs to sanity-check simulation metrics. I'm also figuring out tooling setup — writing pyproject.toml manually and running tests via uv rather than uv init.

Once that's running I'll tune the simulation to hit target metrics and log everything into the ruleset page, changelog, and now.md, then answer the open questions. For Q-03, I'm deciding Steam is fine for now with GOG as a fallback, since the risks are mitigated by only updating on launch and keeping a full backup of the game folder on the D: drive for rollback — and I'm considering whether the executable can be launched directly to avoid Steam's auto-update revalidation.

Since CP2077 has no Denuvo on Steam, launching the exe directly (a common modding trick) might bypass forced updates entirely — I'll mark this as a hypothesis (F-019) to test in Phase 0 rather than assume it works.

Here's the dice service. It derives each roll from the committed seed and a labelled purpose, and the verifier recomputes every roll to check it.

I'm setting up a dice module with a Roll dataclass and a commit function that hashes a seed to create a verifiable commitment, laying groundwork for provably fair dice rolls.

I'm drafting the HMAC-based rejection-sampling draw function to avoid modulo bias, then realize purpose strings containing colons could create ambiguity in the message format used for hashing, so I need to rethink how to delimit session, index, purpose, and attempt safely.

Since the index is unique per draw anyway, cross-draw collisions don't matter — I'll just use a safe separator character and forbid it in purpose strings to keep things simple. Now I'm sketching the dice roller class with d10/d6 methods, a reveal method exposing the seed, and an export_log method producing session id, commit, and roll records, plus a verify_log function that checks for commit mismatches and value mismatches.

I'm also planning a CLI with verify and new commands, confirming rolls get indexed by global sequence since order matters in the event log. For simulation speed I'll add a FastDice class wrapping random.Random with the same interface but explicitly non-provable, deciding whether it belongs in the dice module or sim module. Then I move to the rules config, planning a RulesConfig dataclass loaded from a TOML file that serves as the single source of truth.

Still writing config defaults...

Defining the data model...

MEAT doesn't matter since enemies just die at 0 HP, no death saves needed for them. I'm also sketching out the enemy data fields: HP, armor points for body/head, weapon, status, cover state, pinned/taunted conditions, injuries, per-encounter ability tracking, and action economy (bosses get 2 actions per turn).

Now I'm defining how injuries translate into stat penalties and bleed damage per turn, then designing the core Encounter state structure holding combatants, ranges between them, turn order, round/blackout tracking, and victory/wipe conditions. I'm also setting up an event-sourced system where state changes are represented as typed events (initiative set, turn started, damage dealt, etc.) applied through a single handler function.

Defining more event types...

For event sourcing correctness, I'm making sure resolve() only mutates state by applying emitted events through a single apply() function, so replaying the ledger from a fresh state reproduces the same outcome — which I can verify with a replay property test.

For the turn flow, I'm sketching the loop: start() rolls initiative and emits the opening events, then each turn begin_turn() handles death saves and checks if the actor can act, legal_actions()/resolve() handle the actor's choice, and end_turn() advances turn order, bumping the round and checking for victory or wipe conditions. I'm now writing next_turn() to advance the turn and report whether the next actor is able to act.

Flatlining characters still get a death save but skip acting, so advance() needs to loop through actors: skip dead or fled ones silently, run death saves for flatlining ones, and for active actors apply start-of-turn effects like bleed or pinned decrement before returning the first actor who's still alive and able to act. Round wraparound triggers blackout decrement and a round-start event, and I need to check end conditions after each event batch. Enemies dropping to 0 HP just go straight to dead rather than triggering death saves.

For win/loss conditions: victory happens when all enemies are dead or fled, while a wipe occurs when the whole party is dead or flatlining — though if the party still wins before everyone dies out, flatlining members likely need to be stabilized post-encounter rather than left to keep rolling death saves indefinitely.

I should also account for a round cap mechanic where a prolonged fight becomes a stalemate and the party retreats, which should be tracked as its own outcome category in the metrics.

For attack actions, I'm defining the ranged-vs-melee resolution: each party weapon's damage dice, the to-hit roll against a difficulty based on range band and target cover, with modifiers for wounds, pinning, aiming, overclocking, and enemy blackout effects, plus crit detection when multiple dice show sixes.

For damage resolution, crits add a direct bonus plus an injury effect for party targets, hit location depends on whether the attack was aimed, and armor reduces incoming damage with headshots doubling the penetrating loss and chipping away soak. I'm also adding the spike/glitch rule where a natural 10 or 1 on the roll adds or subtracts an extra d10.

For suppression, I'm having the attacker spend an action to force a save against a fixed difficulty rather than rolling an attack roll themselves, with failure resulting in the target being pinned for a round with an accuracy penalty.

I'm working through the remaining special actions: taking cover, the Solo's overclock for two penalized attacks, the Netrunner's blackout and short abilities tied to a hacking skill check with once-per-encounter limits, and the Tech's patch and stabilize abilities that use a repair skill check to heal or revive downed allies, factoring in medkit bonuses and persistent death-save counts.

Then I'm deciding stabilization should stay Tech-exclusive rather than allowing others at a penalty, since that makes the Tech role critical and adds tension if they go down. I'm also defining deploy_cover for the Tech to upgrade an ally to full cover once per encounter, and taunt for the Face, which forces an enemy to target them on a successful talk check against the enemy's resolve.

Taunt should be at-will since it's the Face's core action, even though they can still attack with their heavy pistol instead. Favors are once per gig and get skipped in non-simulated runs with a note. For enemy AI, I'm setting up basic attack behavior, soldiers taking cover in round one if exposed, bosses getting two actions, and trying to settle on what the Elite's special trick should be — leaning toward a flashbang-style ability that debuffs the party rather than a grenade or aimed shot.

I'm settling on Elite having a once-per-encounter aimed attack with a bonus to hit, and the Boss having a signature "Rampage" move that hits every living party member at a penalty. Mooks will flee once no stronger enemies remain and their hp drops low enough, checked at the start of their turn. For targeting logic, I'm scoring potential targets based on whether they're being taunted (forcing focus on the Face), how wounded they are, whether they have cover, and whether they're already down — weighting enemies away from finishing off flatlined targets unless configured otherwise.

I'm also deciding to break ties deterministically with a small seeded dice draw per enemy so results stay provable, and separating that rule-dice from a separate RNG stream used purely for simulated party bot policy decisions — like Techs prioritizing stabilizing or patching the most damaged ally, and Netrunners leaning toward blackout or shorting out the highest-HP enemy early in a fight.

Rounding out the rest of the crowd policy: Faces taunt when a squishy ally is low, Solos overclock or go for aimed headshots against bosses otherwise focus-firing the weakest enemy, everyone has a chance to take cover round one, and there's a 15% chaos-noise chance of picking a random legal action instead. I'm also sketching the per-gig metrics to track — deaths, wipes, rounds, stalemates, and impact points awarded for damage, successful stabilizes, patches, taunts, and suppressions.

Now I'm working out gig structure: parties carry HP, injuries, and SP chips across encounters within a gig but heal fully between gigs, dead characters just mean a thinner roster rather than a swap-in. I'm defining encounter templates (street, squad, elite, boss) with specific enemy counts, and building gigs out of two encounters drawn from those pools, plus setting up randomized engagement ranges.

I'm also roughing out stat blocks for the party archetypes—Solo, Net, Tech, Face—each with their own attribute spreads, signature weapons, and armor SP values, while setting default cover randomization for each combatant.

Computing HP totals from MEAT scores (Solo 50, Net 35, Tech 45, Face 40) and checking enemy weapon damage dice against party SP thresholds to see how much average damage mooks and soldiers deal per hit.

Running rough hit-probability estimates for enemy attacks against our DV plus cover, and for our own attacks against enemy defenses, to gauge whether lethality feels right. I'll let the actual simulation confirm these numbers before tuning the season0.toml config.

Tuning target: deaths per gig around 25–35%, wipe rate under 3%, combats lasting 4–6 rounds. I'm laying out the file structure for the arcade package (dice, rules, sim modules plus tests and config) and starting to write the core event model with an Event dataclass and an apply function to process state changes.

For replay testing, I'm planning to deep-copy the initial encounter snapshot, apply every event to that copy, then compare against the live state. Turn and round progression gets tracked through dedicated events, and I'm defining the combatant stats and status constants like ALIVE, FLATLINING, DEAD, and FLED as I build out model.py.

Still writing data models...

Adding a temperament field and helper properties for wounded status and action eligibility. Now I'm sketching an injuries table mapping roll results to named injuries with stat penalties and bleed effects.

Thinking through patch/stabilize mechanics: gut shot bleeds each turn until patched, with patching simply removing it from the injury list. Moving on to designing the Encounter dataclass with combatants, range tracking between pairs, and turn order.

Now I'm sketching out the Action dataclass covering the various move types—attacks, suppression, cover, overclock, taunts, and enemy-specific moves like rampage and lock-on.

I'm starting the Engine class, which wraps the rules config and dice roller, with an event-emission helper that applies and records each event for replay. I'm working through how encounter start should reset each combatant's per-fight state—used actions, death saves, pinned/taunted flags, cover—while making sure that reset itself is captured as a proper event so replays stay consistent.

Now I'm defining initiative rolls, sorting combatants by rolled score with GHOST and solo bonuses applied, breaking ties with secondary draws, then emitting the resulting turn order. For advancing the encounter, I'm handling the loop that detects when the pointer moves past the last combatant or a new round begins, emitting a round-started event and updating round count, pointer, and any blackout counter that persists across rounds.

The logic also checks for a max-round stalemate ending condition, and when selecting the next actor it emits a turn-started event -- skipping silently over dead or fled combatants without emitting an event since pointer updates happen naturally on the next valid turn.

Still working through pinning logic... I need to decide how pinned status decrements—whether it applies for exactly one turn then clears, tracked via a consumed flag or a round counter, since doing it at start versus end of turn changes when the attack penalty actually applies.

Taunt clears when the target's next action resolves. For the engine loop, I'm sketching the turn structure: find the next actable combatant, compute legal actions, validate and dispatch a resolved action, then check for end conditions. For bosses with multiple actions per turn, I'll track actions_left set at turn start and decremented via an "action.spent" event, with legal_actions returning empty once exhausted so the orchestrator advances properly.

For determining encounter end, victory happens when no enemies remain alive, which also triggers stabilizing any flatlining party members via "extraction" rather than letting them die. A full wipe occurs when no party members are alive at all -- all flatlining members then die since there's no one left to stabilize them. For stalemates from hitting max rounds, the party escapes and flatlining members get the same stabilization treatment as in victory. Now I'm moving into writing the attack resolution function itself.

Writing attack resolution logic...

I'm defining how the check computes totals: rolling a d10 with exploding bonus on a 10 or penalty on a 1, adding stats adjusted for injuries, specialty bonuses, and situational mods to compare against the difficulty value. I'm consolidating the stat-penalty logic for injuries and wounded status into the single check function.

For damage, I'm working out how to roll damage dice, count sixes for crits, apply armor soak by location (reduced for head/body unless the hit bypasses armor), multiply head shots, add crit bonuses, and emit the resulting damage event.

Then I still need to handle HP and SP updates from that loss, roll injuries for party crits, and transition status when HP hits zero -- enemies die outright, while party members go to flatlining first and only suffer a death save if they take further damage while already at zero.

Death saves compute a threshold from MEAT plus a configured offset minus prior saves, roll a d10 where a natural 10 or exceeding the threshold means failure, emit the result event, and apply death count plus a DEAD status change on failure. I'm keeping MEAT raw rather than adjusting for injuries, and now I need to work out stabilization using the Tech skill against a stabilize difficulty value.

Stabilizing adds a medkit bonus if available, consumes the medkit regardless of outcome, and on success sets the target to ALIVE with 1 HP and clears the gut-shot condition. Patching similarly rolls WRENCH against a patch difficulty to heal and mark patched without consuming resources on failure, while deploy_cover and take_cover just toggle cover states for allies or self, and suppress has the target roll a GHOST save against a suppression difficulty.

Failing the suppress save adds a pinned stack, provided the attacker has a ranged weapon. I'm also laying out the remaining abilities: overclock gives Solos two attacks at a penalty, blackout and short_circuit let Netrunners roll JACK against enemy defenses for disabling effects or direct damage, taunt has Faces roll TALK to redirect enemy attention, and I'm starting on enemy special abilities like the Elite's lock_on attack bonus.

Boss rampage hits every living party member at a penalty, and taunted enemies are restricted to attacking their taunter until that action resolves, at which point the taunt clears. I'm now working out the legal action lists — ranged attacks and suppress for party members, cover options, and the general attack/take_cover/special pattern for enemies.

Since flatlining party members are rarely valid targets (enemies mostly target the living, with rampage also restricted to living targets), I'm adding a config knob for whether enemies can target downed allies, with a heavy AI scoring penalty by default so it almost never happens unless explicitly enabled.

For simulation, I'm building a policy module that uses the engine's legal actions plus a seeded RNG for decision noise, then running many gigs across encounter templates—carrying party state like HP, stamina, and injuries between encounters while excluding the dead—and logging metrics like round counts and outcomes per encounter.

I also need per-gig metrics like death rates and wipe rates, plus per-seat impact scores derived from combat events: damage dealt, stabilizes, heals, and control effects like taunts, pins, and blackouts, which means I need to make sure each event records its source actor. Once that's tracked, I'll print a results table comparing against target thresholds, then start writing the actual code files beginning with config.py.

from .service import Dice, FastDice, Roll, commit_of, verify_log

__all__ = ["Dice", "FastDice", "Roll", "commit_of", "verify_log"]

"""Dice CLI.

python -m arcade.dice new                         print a fresh seed and its commitment
python -m arcade.dice verify LOG.json SEED_HEX    check a published roll log against a revealed seed
"""

import json
import secrets
import sys

from .service import commit_of, verify_log


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) >= 1 and argv[0] == "new":
        seed = secrets.token_bytes(32)
        print(f"seed   {seed.hex()}\ncommit {commit_of(seed)}")
        return 0
    if len(argv) == 3 and argv[0] == "verify":
        with open(argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            exported = json.load(fh)
        problems = verify_log(argv[2], exported)
        for p in problems:
            print(f"FAIL  {p}")
        if not problems:
            print(f"OK  {len(exported['rolls'])} rolls verified against commit {exported['commit'][:16]}…")
        return 1 if problems else 0
    print(__doc__)
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Every tunable number in the ruleset (wiki/design/ruleset.md). Seasons override via TOML."""

from __future__ import annotations

import tomllib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields, replace
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RulesConfig:
    range_dv: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=lambda: {"close": 12, "mid": 15, "far": 18})
    cover_bonus: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=lambda: {"none": 0, "half": 2, "full": 4})
    wounded_penalty: int = 2
    aimed_head_penalty: int = 6
    head_multiplier: int = 2
    crit_six_count: int = 2
    crit_bonus: int = 5
    hp_base: int = 15
    hp_per_meat: int = 5
    death_save_offset: int = 1
    stabilize_dv: int = 13
    medkit_bonus: int = 2
    patch_dv: int = 12
    patch_dice: int = 2
    suppress_dv: int = 15
    pinned_penalty: int = 2
    blackout_dv: int = 13
    blackout_penalty: int = 2
    blackout_rounds: int = 2
    short_dv: int = 15
    short_dice: int = 2
    overclock_penalty: int = 2
    lock_on_bonus: int = 4
    rampage_penalty: int = 2
    taunt_resolve: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=lambda: {"Mook": 10, "Soldier": 12, "Elite": 14, "Boss": 16})
    solo_initiative_bonus: int = 2
    mook_flee_hp: int = 5
    max_rounds: int = 12
    downed_target_penalty: int = 100

    def merged(self, overrides: dict) -> RulesConfig:
        known = {f.name for f in fields(self)}
        unknown = set(overrides) - known
        if unknown:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown rules keys: {sorted(unknown)}")
        merged = {}
        for key, value in overrides.items():
            current = getattr(self, key)
            merged[key] = {**current, **value} if isinstance(current, dict) else value
        return replace(self, **merged)


def load(path: str | Path | None = None) -> RulesConfig:
    base = RulesConfig()
    if path is None:
        return base
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return base.merged(tomllib.load(fh).get("rules", {}))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

STATS = ("IRON", "BLADE", "GHOST", "JACK", "WRENCH", "TALK", "MEAT")
SEATS = ("Solo", "Netrunner", "Tech", "Face")
TIERS = ("Mook", "Soldier", "Elite", "Boss")

ALIVE, FLATLINING, DEAD, FLED = "ALIVE", "FLATLINING", "DEAD", "FLED"
COVER = ("none", "half", "full")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Weapon:
    name: str
    dice: int
    close_only: bool = False


WEAPONS = {
    "light_pistol": Weapon("light_pistol", 2),
    "heavy_pistol": Weapon("heavy_pistol", 3),
    "rifle": Weapon("rifle", 4),
    "shotgun": Weapon("shotgun", 5, close_only=True),
}

# d6 → (injury, stat penalties ("*" = all checks), HP bleed at the start of each own turn until patched)
INJURIES: dict[int, tuple[str, dict[str, int], int]] = {
    1: ("glass_eye", {"IRON": -2}, 0),
    2: ("cracked_ribs", {"*": -1}, 0),
    3: ("burned_hand", {"IRON": -1, "BLADE": -2}, 0),
    4: ("concussion", {"JACK": -2, "TALK": -2}, 0),
    5: ("shrapnel_leg", {"GHOST": -2}, 0),
    6: ("gut_shot", {}, 2),
}
INJURY_BY_NAME = {name: (penalties, bleed) for name, penalties, bleed in INJURIES.values()}


@dataclass
class Combatant:
    id: str
    name: str
    side: str
    role: str
    stats: dict[str, int]
    signature: str
    specialty: int
    max_hp: int
    hp: int
    sp_body: int
    sp_head: int
    weapon: str
    node_cover: str = "half"
    cover: str = "none"
    status: str = ALIVE
    death_saves: int = 0
    pinned: int = 0
    suppressed: bool = False
    taunted_by: str | None = None
    injuries: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    used: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    patched: bool = False
    medkits: int = 0
    actions_per_turn: int = 1
    actions_left: int = 0
    temperament: str = "steady"

    @property
    def wounded(self) -> bool:
        return self.hp <= self.max_hp // 2

    def stat(self, name: str) -> int:
        value = self.stats.get(name, 0)
        for injury in self.injuries:
            penalties, _ = INJURY_BY_NAME[injury]
            value += penalties.get(name, 0) + penalties.get("*", 0)
        return value

    @property
    def bleed(self) -> int:
        return sum(INJURY_BY_NAME[i][1] for i in self.injuries)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Action:
    kind: str
    actor: str
    target: str | None = None

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.kind}->{self.target}" if self.target else self.kind


@dataclass
class Encounter:
    id: str
    combatants: dict[str, Combatant]
    ranges: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    default_range: str = "mid"
    order: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    round: int = 0
    pointer: int = -1
    blackout: int = 0
    result: str | None = None

    def range_between(self, a: str, b: str) -> str:
        return self.ranges.get(range_key(a, b), self.default_range)

    def side(self, side: str) -> list[Combatant]:
        return [c for c in self.combatants.values() if c.side == side]

    def current(self) -> Combatant | None:
        if 0 <= self.pointer < len(self.order):
            return self.combatants[self.order[self.pointer]]
        return None


def range_key(a: str, b: str) -> str:
    return "|".join(sorted((a, b)))

"""Events are the only way encounter state changes (ADR-007). `apply` is the fold step."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .model import ALIVE, DEAD, Encounter


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    type: str
    data: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def apply(enc: Encounter, ev: Event) -> None:
    d = ev.data
    c = enc.combatants.get(d.get("target") or d.get("actor") or "")
    match ev.type:
        case "encounter.started":
            enc.round, enc.pointer, enc.blackout, enc.result = 0, -1, 0, None
            for x in enc.combatants.values():
                x.death_saves, x.pinned, x.suppressed, x.taunted_by = 0, 0, False, None
                x.used, x.patched, x.actions_left = [], False, 0
        case "initiative.set":
            enc.order = list(d["order"])
        case "round.started":
            enc.round, enc.pointer = d["round"], -1
            if d["round"] > 1:
                enc.blackout = max(0, enc.blackout - 1)
        case "turn.started":
            enc.pointer = d["index"]
            c.suppressed = c.pinned > 0
            c.pinned = max(0, c.pinned - 1)
            c.actions_left = c.actions_per_turn
        case "action.spent":
            c.actions_left -= 1
            if c.side == "enemy":
                c.taunted_by = None
        case "ability.used":
            c.used.append(d["ability"])
        case "damage.applied":
            c.hp = max(0, c.hp - d["loss"])
            if d["chip"]:
                if d["location"] == "head":
                    c.sp_head = max(0, c.sp_head - 1)
                else:
                    c.sp_body = max(0, c.sp_body - 1)
        case "healed":
            c.hp = min(c.max_hp, c.hp + d["amount"])
            c.patched = True
            if "gut_shot" in c.injuries:
                c.injuries.remove("gut_shot")
        case "bled":
            c.hp = max(0, c.hp - d["amount"])
        case "injury.added":
            c.injuries.append(d["injury"])
        case "status.changed":
            c.status = d["status"]
            if d["status"] == DEAD:
                c.hp = 0
        case "death_save":
            c.death_saves += 1
        case "stabilized":
            c.status, c.hp = ALIVE, max(1, c.hp)
            if "gut_shot" in c.injuries:
                c.injuries.remove("gut_shot")
        case "medkit.used":
            c.medkits -= 1
        case "cover.changed":
            c.cover = d["cover"]
        case "pinned":
            c.pinned = max(c.pinned, 1)
        case "taunted":
            c.taunted_by = d["by"]
        case "blackout":
            enc.blackout = d["rounds"]
        case "encounter.ended":
            enc.result = d["result"]
        case "attack.rolled" | "check.rolled" | "initiative.rolled":
            pass
        case _:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown event type {ev.type}")

"""Crowd policy: what a plurality vote of a distracted audience plausibly picks. Not authoritative."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

from ..rules.model import ALIVE, FLATLINING, Action, Encounter


def heuristic(enc: Encounter, a: Action) -> float:
    c = enc.combatants[a.actor]
    t = enc.combatants.get(a.target) if a.target else None
    allies_wounded = sum(1 for p in enc.side("party") if p.status == ALIVE and p.wounded)
    threat = {"Mook": 0, "Soldier": 1, "Elite": 2, "Boss": 3}.get(t.role, 0) if t is not None else 0
    match a.kind:
        case "attack":
            return 5 + (2 if t.wounded else 0) + (1 if t.cover == "none" else 0) - 0.3 * threat
        case "aimed_shot":
            return 2 + threat * 0.5
        case "suppress":
            return 2.5 + threat * 0.5
        case "take_cover":
            return 6.5 if c.cover == "none" else 3
        case "overclock":
            return 7 + threat
        case "blackout":
            return 8 if enc.round <= 2 else 5
        case "short_circuit":
            return 6 + threat
        case "stabilize":
            return 12
        case "patch":
            missing = (t.max_hp - t.hp) / t.max_hp
            return 2 + 8 * missing
        case "deploy_cover":
            return 4 + (3 if t.wounded else 0) + (1 if t.cover == "none" else 0)
        case "taunt":
            return 3 + 1.5 * threat + allies_wounded
    return 1


class CrowdPolicy:
    def __init__(self, rng: random.Random, chaos: float = 0.15, noise: float = 1.5) -> None:
        self.rng, self.chaos, self.noise = rng, chaos, noise

    def __call__(self, enc: Encounter, options: list[Action]) -> Action:
        if self.rng.random() < self.chaos:
            return self.rng.choice(options)
        return max(options, key=lambda a: heuristic(enc, a) + self.rng.gauss(0, self.noise))


def flatlining(enc: Encounter) -> int:
    return sum(1 for p in enc.side("party") if p.status == FLATLINING)

"""Monte Carlo gigs against the Season 0 balance targets (wiki/design/ruleset.md)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
import statistics
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ..dice import FastDice
from ..rules import ai
from ..rules.config import RulesConfig
from ..rules.engine import Engine
from ..rules.model import ALIVE, DEAD, Combatant, Encounter, range_key
from ..rules.roster import enemy, party

TARGETS = {
    "rounds_per_encounter": (4.0, 6.0),
    "p_death_per_gig": (0.25, 0.35),
    "p_wipe_per_gig": (0.0, 0.03),
}

OPENERS = {"street": ["Mook", "Mook", "Mook", "Soldier"], "squad": ["Soldier", "Soldier", "Mook", "Mook"]}
CLOSERS = {"elite": ["Elite", "Soldier", "Soldier"], "boss": ["Boss", "Mook", "Mook"]}
RANGES = (("close", 0.25), ("mid", 0.55), ("far", 0.20))
COVERS = (("none", 0.2), ("half", 0.5), ("full", 0.3))


@dataclass
class GigResult:
    shape: str
    deaths: int
    wiped: bool
    rounds: list[int]
    results: list[str]
    damage_by: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)
    actions: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)


def _pick(rng: random.Random, table) -> str:
    names, weights = zip(*table)
    return rng.choices(names, weights)[0]


def build_encounter(eid: str, crew: list[Combatant], tiers: list[str], rng: random.Random) -> Encounter:
    foes = []
    for i, tier in enumerate(tiers):
        foe = enemy(tier, f"{tier.lower()}{i}")
        foe.node_cover = _pick(rng, COVERS)
        foe.cover = foe.node_cover
        foes.append(foe)
    for p in crew:
        p.node_cover, p.cover = _pick(rng, COVERS), "none"
    ranges = {range_key(p.id, f.id): _pick(rng, RANGES) for p in crew for f in foes}
    return Encounter(eid, {c.id: c for c in [*crew, *foes]}, ranges)


def play_gig(cfg: RulesConfig, seed: int, crowd_chaos: float = 0.15) -> GigResult:
    rng = random.Random(seed ^ 0x5EED)
    dice = FastDice(seed)
    crew = party(cfg)
    opener, closer = rng.choice(list(OPENERS)), rng.choice(list(CLOSERS))
    crowd = __import__("arcade.sim.policy", fromlist=["CrowdPolicy"]).CrowdPolicy(rng, chaos=crowd_chaos)
    out = GigResult(f"{opener}+{closer}", 0, False, [], [])
    for n, tiers in enumerate((OPENERS[opener], CLOSERS[closer])):
        if not any(p.status == ALIVE for p in crew):
            break
        enc = build_encounter(f"gig{seed}:e{n}", crew, tiers, rng)
        engine = Engine(cfg, dice)
        if n > 0:
            engine.breather(enc)
        engine.start(enc)
        while (actor := engine.advance(enc)) is not None:
            while options := engine.legal_actions(enc, actor):
                action = crowd(enc, options) if enc.combatants[actor].side == "party" else ai.choose(engine, enc, actor)
                if enc.combatants[actor].side == "party":
                    out.actions[f"{enc.combatants[actor].role}:{action.kind}"] += 1
                engine.resolve(enc, action)
        for ev in engine.events:
            if ev.type == "damage.applied" and enc.combatants[ev.data["target"]].side == "enemy":
                out.damage_by[enc.combatants[ev.data["source"]].role] += ev.data["loss"]
        out.rounds.append(enc.round)
        out.results.append(enc.result)
        if enc.result == "wipe":
            out.wiped = True
            break
    out.deaths = sum(1 for p in crew if p.status == DEAD)
    return out


def summarize(results: list[GigResult]) -> dict:
    rounds = [r for g in results for r in g.rounds]
    party_damage = Counter()
    actions = Counter()
    for g in results:
        party_damage.update({k: v for k, v in g.damage_by.items() if k in ("Solo", "Netrunner", "Tech", "Face")})
        actions.update(g.actions)
    total_dmg = sum(party_damage.values()) or 1
    by_shape: dict[str, list[GigResult]] = {}
    for g in results:
        by_shape.setdefault(g.shape, []).append(g)
    return {
        "gigs": len(results),
        "rounds_per_encounter": statistics.mean(rounds),
        "rounds_p90": sorted(rounds)[int(0.9 * (len(rounds) - 1))],
        "p_death_per_gig": sum(g.deaths > 0 for g in results) / len(results),
        "p_wipe_per_gig": sum(g.wiped for g in results) / len(results),
        "mean_deaths": statistics.mean(g.deaths for g in results),
        "stalemates": sum(r == "stalemate" for g in results for r in g.results),
        "damage_share": {k: party_damage[k] / total_dmg for k in ("Solo", "Netrunner", "Tech", "Face")},
        "by_shape": {s: {"n": len(gs), "p_death": sum(g.deaths > 0 for g in gs) / len(gs),
                         "p_wipe": sum(g.wiped for g in gs) / len(gs)} for s, gs in sorted(by_shape.items())},
        "top_actions": actions.most_common(16),
    }


def run(cfg: RulesConfig, gigs: int, seed: int, crowd_chaos: float = 0.15) -> dict:
    return summarize([play_gig(cfg, seed * 1_000_003 + i, crowd_chaos) for i in range(gigs)])


def verdict(summary: dict) -> list[str]:
    lines = []
    for key, (lo, hi) in TARGETS.items():
        value = summary[key]
        lines.append(f"{'PASS' if lo <= value <= hi else 'MISS'} {key} = {value:.3f} (target {lo}-{hi})")
    return lines

from .run import TARGETS, play_gig, run, verdict

"""python -m arcade.sim [--gigs N] [--seed S] [--rules content/rules/season0.toml] [--chaos 0.15] [--json]"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from ..rules.config import load
from .run import run, verdict


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="arcade.sim")
    ap.add_argument("--gigs", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--rules", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--chaos", type=float, default=0.15)
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    summary = run(load(args.rules), args.gigs, args.seed, args.chaos)
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
        return 0
    for line in verdict(summary):
        print(line)
    print(f"rounds p90 = {summary['rounds_p90']}, mean deaths/gig = {summary['mean_deaths']:.2f}, "
          f"stalemates = {summary['stalemates']}")
    print("damage share: " + ", ".join(f"{k} {v:.0%}" for k, v in summary["damage_share"].items()))
    for shape, s in summary["by_shape"].items():
        print(f"  {shape:14s} n={s['n']:5d} p_death={s['p_death']:.2f} p_wipe={s['p_wipe']:.3f}")
    print("top party actions: " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in summary["top_actions"][:10]))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    def merged(self, overrides: dict) -> RulesConfig:
        known = {f.name for f in fields(self)}
        unknown = set(overrides) - known
        if unknown:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown rules keys: {sorted(unknown)}")
        return replace(self, **{k: _deep_merge(getattr(self, k), v) for k, v in overrides.items()})


def _deep_merge(current, value):
    if isinstance(current, dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
        out = copy.deepcopy(current)
        for k, v in value.items():
            out[k] = _deep_merge(out[k], v) if k in out else v
        return out
    return value


def load(path: str | Path | None = None) -> RulesConfig:
    base = RulesConfig()
    if path is None:
        return base
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return base.merged(tomllib.load(fh).get("rules", {}))

import argparse

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="arcade.sim")
    ap.add_argument("--gigs", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--rules", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--chaos", type=float, default=0.15, help="share of crowd decisions that are uniformly random")
    ap.add_argument("--ablate", action="store_true", help="rerun with each seat idle to measure seat impact")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    summary = run(load(args.rules), args.gigs, args.seed, args.chaos, args.ablate)
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
        return 0
    for line in verdict(summary):

    print(f"rounds p90 = {summary['rounds_p90']}, mean deaths/gig = {summary['mean_deaths']:.2f}, "
          f"loss/gig = {summary['loss']:.3f}")

    if "seat_impact_share" in summary:

            f"{k} +{summary['seat_loss_if_idle'][k]:.2f} ({v:.0%})" for k, v in summary["seat_impact_share"].items()))

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":

from arcade.dice import Dice, verify_log

SEED = bytes(range(32))


def test_same_seed_same_rolls():
    a, b = Dice(SEED, "s1"), Dice(SEED, "s1")
    assert [a.d10("x") for _ in range(50)] == [b.d10("x") for _ in range(50)]


def test_session_and_purpose_change_the_stream():
    base = [Dice(SEED, "s1").d10("x") for _ in range(1)]
    rolls_a = [Dice(SEED, "s1").roll(1000, "x")]
    rolls_b = [Dice(SEED, "s2").roll(1000, "x")]
    rolls_c = [Dice(SEED, "s1").roll(1000, "y")]
    assert base
    assert rolls_a != rolls_b or rolls_a != rolls_c


def test_verify_accepts_honest_log():
    d = Dice(SEED, "show-1")
    for i in range(200):
        d.roll(6 if i % 2 else 10, f"p{i}")
    assert verify_log(SEED.hex(), d.export()) == []


def test_verify_catches_tampering_and_wrong_seed():
    d = Dice(SEED, "show-1")
    for i in range(20):
        d.d10(f"p{i}")
    log = d.export()
    log["rolls"][5]["value"] = log["rolls"][5]["value"] % 10 + 1
    assert any("#5" in p for p in verify_log(SEED.hex(), log))
    assert any("commitment" in p for p in verify_log(bytes(32).hex(), d.export()))


def test_faces_are_uniform():
    d = Dice(SEED, "uniform")
    n = 20_000
    counts = Counter(d.d10("u") for _ in range(n))
    expected = n / 10
    chi2 = sum((counts[f] - expected) ** 2 / expected for f in range(1, 11))
    assert set(counts) == set(range(1, 11))
    assert chi2 < 27.9  # p = 0.001 for 9 degrees of freedom

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Dice(SEED).roll(1, "x")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

import copy
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from hypothesis import given, settings
from hypothesis import strategies as st

from arcade.dice import Dice
from arcade.rules import ALIVE, DEAD, FLATLINING, Action, Encounter, Engine, IllegalAction, RulesConfig, apply, load
from arcade.rules import ai, enemy, party
from arcade.rules.model import range_key

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CFG = load(ROOT / "content/rules/season0.toml")


class ScriptedDice(Dice):
    """Returns queued values; falls back to 5 so tests only script the rolls they care about."""

    def __init__(self, values=()):
        super().__init__(bytes(32), "test")
        self.queue = list(values)

    def roll(self, faces, purpose):
        value = self.queue.pop(0) if self.queue else 5
        assert 1 <= value <= faces, (purpose, value, faces)
        return value


def make_encounter(cfg=CFG, tiers=("Soldier", "Mook", "Mook"), rng_range="mid"):
    crew = party(cfg)
    foes = [enemy(t, f"{t.lower()}{i}", cfg) for i, t in enumerate(tiers)]
    for f in foes:
        f.node_cover = f.cover = "half"
    ranges = {range_key(p.id, f.id): rng_range for p in crew for f in foes}
    return Encounter("t", {c.id: c for c in [*crew, *foes]}, ranges)


def play(engine, enc, party_choice=lambda opts: opts[0]):
    engine.start(enc)
    while (actor := engine.advance(enc)) is not None:
        while opts := engine.legal_actions(enc, actor):
            c = enc.combatants[actor]
            engine.resolve(enc, ai.choose(engine, enc, actor) if c.side == "enemy" else party_choice(opts))
    return enc


def snapshot(enc):
    return asdict(enc)


def test_replay_reproduces_final_state():
    initial = make_encounter(tiers=("Elite", "Soldier", "Mook"))
    pristine = copy.deepcopy(initial)
    engine = Engine(CFG, Dice(bytes(range(32)), "replay"))
    final = play(engine, initial)
    assert final.result in {"victory", "wipe", "stalemate"}
    for ev in engine.events:
        apply(pristine, ev)
    assert snapshot(pristine) == snapshot(final)


def test_same_seed_same_events():
    runs = []
    for _ in range(2):
        engine = Engine(CFG, Dice(bytes(range(32)), "det"))
        play(engine, make_encounter())

def test_stabilize_returns_to_alive_at_one_hp():

    from arcade.rules.events import Event

    apply(enc, Event("turn.started", {"actor": "mook0", "index": idx}))
    assert engine.legal_actions(enc, "mook0") == []


def test_heat_degrades_cover_from_heat_round():

    engine = Engine(cfg, Dice(bytes(range(32)), "heat"))
    engine.start(enc)
    for c in enc.combatants.values():
        c.cover = c.node_cover = "full"
    while enc.round < 2 and enc.result is None:
        actor = engine.advance(enc)
        if actor is None:
            break
        while opts := engine.legal_actions(enc, actor):
            engine.resolve(enc, opts[-1])
    assert any(ev.type == "heat.rose" for ev in engine.events)
    assert all(c.node_cover != "full" for c in enc.combatants.values())


def test_config_rejects_unknown_keys_and_deep_merges():
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        RulesConfig().merged({"nope": 1})
    merged = RulesConfig().merged({"seats": {"Solo": {"stats": {"IRON": 3}}}})
    assert merged.seats["Solo"]["stats"]["IRON"] == 3
    assert merged.seats["Solo"]["stats"]["MEAT"] == RulesConfig().seats["Solo"]["stats"]["MEAT"]
    assert RulesConfig().seats["Solo"]["stats"]["IRON"] == 8


@settings(max_examples=40, deadline=None)
@given(seed=st.binary(min_size=16, max_size=32),
       tiers=st.lists(st.sampled_from(["Mook", "Soldier", "Elite", "Boss"]), min_size=1, max_size=4),
       rng_range=st.sampled_from(["close", "mid", "far"]),
       pick=st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=7))
def test_any_encounter_terminates_with_sane_state(seed, tiers, rng_range, pick):
    enc = make_encounter(tiers=tuple(tiers), rng_range=rng_range)
    engine = Engine(CFG, Dice(seed, "prop"))
    play(engine, enc, party_choice=lambda opts: opts[pick % len(opts)])
    assert enc.result in {"victory", "wipe", "stalemate"}
    assert enc.round <= CFG.max_rounds
    for c in enc.combatants.values():
        assert 0 <= c.hp <= c.max_hp
        assert c.status != FLATLINING
        if c.status == DEAD:
            assert c.hp == 0
    dead_once = set()
    for ev in engine.events:
        target = ev.data.get("target")
        if ev.type == "status.changed" and ev.data["status"] == DEAD:
            dead_once.add(target)
        elif ev.type in ("healed", "stabilized") and target in dead_once:
            pytest.fail(f"{target} acted on after death")

---
type: design
title: Ruleset v0 — RED-shaped homebrew (simulator-tuned, Season 0 candidate)
status: draft
updated: 2026-10-11
depends_on: [ADR-005, ADR-006, ADR-007]
---

# Ruleset v0

Original names and numbers (ADR-005). Code: `arcade/rules/` (engine, events, enemy AI). Every number is a knob:
defaults in `arcade/rules/config.py`, Season 0 overrides in `content/rules/season0.toml`, set by the balance simulator
(`python -m arcade.sim --rules content/rules/season0.toml --ablate`), frozen per season. **The TOML is the source of
truth for numbers; this page explains them.** If they disagree, the TOML wins and this page is stale.

## Stats (7, range 2–8 at creation, cap 10)
IRON (guns) · BLADE (melee) · GHOST (stealth, evasion, initiative) · JACK (netrunning) · WRENCH (tech, medicine, devices) · TALK (social) · MEAT (body, HP, death saves)

A stat already folds in training (there are no separate skills), so DVs sit lower than in RED.

## Check
`d10 + STAT + Specialty (+2 on the seat's signature stat) + modifiers ≥ DV`
- **Spike**: a natural 10 rolls another d10 and adds it. **Glitch**: a natural 1 rolls another d10 and subtracts it.
- Non-combat DV ladder: Easy 8 · Standard 12 · Hard 15 · Severe 18.
- **Wounded** (HP ≤ half): −2 to all checks.
- Every roll is drawn from the provable dice stream with a purpose label (`r3:solo:attack:d10`), so the overlay can show it and anyone can verify it (ADR-006).

## Initiative
`d10 + GHOST` (Solo +2). Ties: higher GHOST, then a dice draw. Rolled once per encounter → initiative rail on the overlay.

## Turn loop
Each round, combatants act in initiative order with 1 action (Boss: 2). Start of turn: flatlining → death save instead of acting;
bleeding injuries tick; pinned → this turn's attacks −2. **Hold** is always legal (the vote-timeout default).

## Ranged combat (node graph)
- Base DV by range band between nodes: **close 8 · mid 11 · far 14**. The crew adds **+2 weapon skill**; enemies use their tier specialty.
- Target cover: half +2, full +4. **Take cover** moves you to your node's best cover (party start in the open).
- **Aimed head shot**: −6 to hit; damage after armor doubled.
- **Suppress**: target makes GHOST vs DV 15 or is **Pinned** (its next turn's attacks −2).
- **Heat**: from round 6, every node's cover drops one step at the start of each round (full → half → none). The scene is
  coming apart; this ends turtling and keeps encounters inside the show clock. Stalemate at round 12 is a failsafe, not a mechanic.
- Melee (not yet in code): opposed `d10 + BLADE` vs `d10 + max(BLADE, GHOST)`.

## Damage and armor
- Weapons: light pistol 2d6 · heavy pistol 3d6 · rifle 4d6 · shotgun 5d6 (close only).
- **Armor (SP)** per location (body, head): damage > SP → HP loses (damage − SP) and that SP drops by 1. Damage ≤ SP → nothing.
- **Critical**: two or more 6s on the damage dice → **+5 HP loss applied after armor** (it never gets soaked), and party
  members roll the injury table (d6: glass eye IRON −2 · cracked ribs all −1 · burned hand IRON −1/BLADE −2 · concussion JACK/TALK −2 · shrapnel leg GHOST −2 · gut shot bleed 2/turn until patched).

## HP and death
- `HP = 15 + 5 × MEAT` (MEAT 5 → 40). Enemies at 0 HP die; Mooks flee at ≤ 5 HP once no leader is standing.
- Party at 0 HP → **FLATLINING**: no actions. Start of each own turn: death save, success if `d10 ≤ MEAT + 1 − n`
  (n = saves already made this encounter); natural 10 always fails. Damage while flatlining forces an extra save. One failure = **permanent death**.
- **Stabilize** (Tech, WRENCH vs DV 13, +2 with a medkit, 2 medkits per gig): back to ALIVE at 1 HP.
- Encounter ends with someone standing → flatlining crew are carried out (stabilized). Nobody standing → they die.
- **Breather** between the encounters of one gig: each surviving crew member heals 2d6.

## Seat abilities
| Seat | Action | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Solo | Overclock (1/encounter) | Two attacks at −2 on one target |
| Netrunner | Blackout (1/encounter) | JACK vs DV 13: enemy attacks −2 for 2 rounds |
| Netrunner | Short circuit (repeatable) | JACK vs DV 15: 2d6 ignoring armor |
| Tech | Patch (each ally once per encounter) | WRENCH vs DV 12: heal 2d6, stops bleeding |
| Tech | Deploy cover (1/encounter) | Ally to full cover |
| Tech | Stabilize | See above |
| Face | Taunt (repeatable, one pending per enemy) | TALK vs resolve (Mook 10 · Soldier 12 · Elite 14 · Boss 16): the enemy loses its next action |

Not yet in code (need scene affordances or gig layer): Netrunner Hijack (take a turret) and Ping (telegraph enemy intent), Face Call a Favor (once per gig).

## Enemies
| Tier | IRON + specialty | HP | SP | Weapon | Trick |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mook | 5 + 0 | 10 | 0 | light pistol | Flees |
| Soldier | 6 + 1 | 18 | 2 | heavy pistol | — |
| Elite | 8 + 2 | 35 | 6 | rifle | Lock-on: one attack at +4 |
| Boss | 7 + 2 | 45 | 5 | rifle | 2 actions/round; Rampage: one attack at −2 on every standing crew member |

Enemy AI (`arcade/rules/ai.py`) = utility scoring over the same legal actions: prefer wounded targets and targets in the open,
avoid finishing the flatlining (−100), lock-on/rampage when they pay. Ties within 2 points are broken by a provable d6, so
enemy choices are deterministic, auditable, and replayable (ADR-007).

## Action generation (planned, replaces per-node `valid_actions` lists)
`options = seat_actions ∩ node_affordances(node.tags) ∩ legal(state)` → ranked → top 4 (always one defensive option).
Scene authors tag nodes (`cover:half`, `console:turret`, `door:weldable`, `vantage`), not actions. Today `legal_actions` implements the `legal(state)` part.

## Balance targets and Season 0 results
Gig = opener (street: 3 Mooks + Soldier, or squad: 2 Soldiers + 2 Mooks) then closer (elite: Elite + 2 Soldiers, or boss: Boss + 2 Mooks),
random range bands (close 25 % / mid 55 % / far 20 %) and node cover. Crowd = noisy heuristic policy, 15 % uniformly random votes.

4,000 gigs, seed 1, 2026-10-11:

| Target | Band | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rounds per encounter | 4–6 | 5.58 (p90 = 8) |
| P(≥ 1 permanent death per gig) | 25–35 % | 27.6 % |
| P(party wipe per gig) | < 3 % | 0.2 % |
| P(stalemate per encounter) | < 1 % | 1.0 % (at the edge) |

By gig shape, death rate is street+elite 15 % · squad+elite 17 % · street+boss 37 % · squad+boss 42 %. Boss gigs being
about 2.5× deadlier is a feature if the gig board shows it (risk vs payout is a crowd choice); see [campaign](campaign.md).

Crowd skill matters, which is what makes voting meaningful: P(death) is 22 % with a perfect crowd, 28 % at 15 % chaos,
35 % at 30 %, and 46 % at 50 % chaos (wipes stay < 3 % even then; rounds rise to 6.5).

**Seat balance (open).** Two ablations, each comparing extra party loss (deaths + 2 × wipe) per gig:
- *Seat power* (the seat only holds): Solo 55 % · Tech 21 % · Netrunner 12 % · Face 12 %.
- *Vote leverage* (the seat's squad votes at random): Solo 37 % · Tech 34 % · Netrunner 15 % · Face 14 %.

The target "every seat ≥ 20 %" is met for Solo and Tech only. Swapping weapons barely moves it; the missing lever is
choice depth for Netrunner and Face (Hijack, Ping, Call a Favor are not modeled yet). Tracked as Q-10.

## Tuning history (v0 pass, 2026-10-11)
1. RED-like DVs (12/15/18) with 2–8 stats: 12-round stalemates, 92 % death, 17 % wipe. Stats already include training, so DVs had to drop.
2. DVs 8/11/14 + 2 weapon skill: still 73 % death; the Boss (SP 13) was immune to pistols and dealt ~156 damage per fight.
3. Enemy armor and accuracy down (SP 0/2/4–6/5): all lifecycle targets pass; boss gigs 4× deadlier than elite gigs; 5 % stalemates.
4. Heat (round 6), Taunt = lose next action, repeatable Short circuit, Solo IRON 8 → 7, Elite up / Boss down: current numbers.

content.text:
B1 is built and committed (`53dc785`): provably fair dice, the rules core and the balance simulator. The Season 0 numbers hit all four balance targets over 4,000 simulated gigs. One goal is still short: Netrunner and Face votes matter less than Solo and Tech votes.

**What's there**
- **Dice** (`arcade/dice`): every roll comes from a secret seed and is labelled (e.g. `r3:solo:attack:d10`). Before the show you publish a fingerprint of the seed; after it, you reveal the seed. `python -m arcade.dice verify` then lets anyone recompute every roll and catch tampering.
- **Rules** (`arcade/rules`): the game state changes only through recorded events. Replaying a fight's events from the starting position reproduces it exactly, which the event-log design depends on.
  - Enemy AI is a fixed scoring system that breaks ties with the same verifiable dice, so enemy choices can be audited too.
  - Every number lives in `content/rules/season0.toml`. That file is now the source of truth, and the ruleset wiki page explains it.
- **Simulator** (`python -m arcade.sim --rules content/rules/season0.toml --ablate`): plays full gigs with a simulated crowd that votes sensibly but with noise, 15% of votes random. `--ablate` reruns with each seat idle or voting randomly, to measure how much that seat matters.
- **Tests:** 21 pass (`uv run pytest`). One generates random fights and checks that every one ends cleanly, with HP in range and no action on the dead.

**Results**

| Target | Goal | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rounds per encounter | 4–6 | 5.6 |
| Gigs with at least one permanent death | 25–35% | 27.6% |
| Gigs where the whole party dies | under 3% | 0.2% |
| Fights that hit the 12-round limit | under 1% | 1.0% (at the edge) |

Crowd skill matters: deaths go from 22% of gigs with a perfect crowd to 46% with a half-random one, while full-party deaths stay under 3%. Boss gigs are about 2.5× deadlier than elite gigs. I'd show that on the gig board as risk versus payout rather than flatten it.

**Rules I changed because the simulator showed problems**
- **Lower difficulty numbers** (8/11/14 by range instead of 12/15/18), plus a +2 weapon skill for the crew. Stats already include training, so the original numbers made the crew miss so often that most fights ran to the round limit.
- **Heat:** from round 6, every position's cover gets worse each round. This stops both sides hiding in cover forever and keeps fights inside the show's time box.
- **Taunt** now makes the enemy lose its next action. It used to just pull fire onto the Face, the most fragile seat.
- **Short circuit** can now be used repeatedly.
- **Hold** is always a legal choice, so a vote that times out has a default.
- **Enemies have much less armor.** The boss's old armor made pistols useless against it.

Each tuning pass, and why, is logged on the wiki ruleset page.

**Still open:** how much a squad's vote changes the outcome splits Solo 37%, Tech 34%, Netrunner 15%, Face 14%, against a goal of at least 20% each. Swapping weapons barely moved it. The likely fix is the abilities the simulator doesn't model yet: Ping, Hijack and Call a Favor. I filed this as Q-10 with a default plan.

The wiki now lists the actual rules events in the contracts page and has updated `now.md` and the log; its checker reports 0 errors.

**Next:** on your side, the Steam install to `D:\SteamLibrary` and the Phase 0 checklist. On mine, B2: show clock, chat parsing, vote counting and a simulated chat crowd, driving these rules. None of that needs the game installed.
